# Knowledge packs: research sweeps served to agents as versioned skills

English | [中文](2026-09-07-knowledge-packs.zh.md)

Status: proposed, first pack landed. Owner: the improvement seam.

## Decision

Knowledge that agents in this harness should have and models do not, such as the state of the art of a dated window, enters the harness as a **knowledge pack**: a directory under `data/knowledge/<pack>/` holding a sourced corpus (`corpus/items.json`, the merged output of dated research sweeps, plus each sweep's briefing) and one skill bundle per theme (`skills/<theme>/SKILL.md`, an authored body, with a generated `references/items.md` listing the corpus items of that theme). A pack is served to agents by the shipped filesystem skill provider with the pack's `skills/` directory as a custom skill root and the default roots excluded, so a composition's catalog is the pack's contents wherever it runs. `data/knowledge/tools/build-pack.mjs` builds a pack from the sweeps, renders the references, validates every frontmatter, and writes a manifest with every file's digest; its `--check` mode is the `verify-knowledge-packs` leaf of `doc-sync`, so a stale pack fails the gate.

## Why a plugin and not a document

Three properties the skill seam already has are the reasons, and none of them is available to a document an agent is told to read.

1. **Identity and provenance.** A loaded skill is addressed by `skillDigest()` over its name, description, routing metadata, and body, and the composition manifest records which generation was in play in every session. A pack is therefore a component: an experiment can pair a session with the pack against one without it or with the previous pack, and the observatory attributes the difference to a digest, not to a prose claim that the agents "had the knowledge".
2. **Scope and policy.** Skills file into the layer of the composition that mounts them and carry an invocation policy per surface, so a pack can be mounted for one preset, one district, or one department without leaking into the host's own skill roots, and a pack meant for judges is not loadable by implementers.
3. **Token and cache economy.** The catalog reaches the model once, as a durable user-role message appended after the reusable prefix, with each theme reduced to its name and a capped description; a body is loaded only when the model calls the `skill` tool and then lives in retained tool history, and the item tables behind it load on demand through the resource guidance. A catalog change appends a replacement rather than rewriting earlier history, so the cached prefix survives edits to the pack. This is what makes knowledge as a plugin cheaper than knowledge in the system prompt: progressive disclosure keeps every request small, and append-only invalidation keeps the KV cache warm. It is the mechanism, not the purpose: the purpose is that the knowledge is a measured, versioned component.

## Mechanism

- `pack.json` names the pack, its window, its sources, and its themes; a theme has kebab-case `id`, a `title`, the item `kinds` it collects, and the `keywords` that select items by tag or by whole word in name and summary. An item may belong to several themes; items no theme selects are listed in the manifest's `counts.unmatched`.
- A sweep is a research agent's output for one source: `items.json` (`id`, `kind`, `name`, `date`, `url`, `summary`, `relevance { goals, seams, role }`, `adopt`, `evidence`, `tags`) and `report.md`. The build validates every item, deduplicates by URL across sources, unions tags and goals, and records which sources reported the item.
- The authored `SKILL.md` body is where the judgement lives: what changed, what Daliesk adopts, rejects, or tests, and how to use the references. Its description must fit the catalog cap (500 characters). The generated `references/items.md` is never edited by hand.
- The composition that proves the seam is `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/knowledge-pack/cordis.yml`: the pack's `skills/` as the only root, a keyless route that reads the catalog, loads the first skill through the `skill` tool, and reports the loaded name. `examples/headless-agent/tests/knowledge-pack.e2e.ts` asserts the catalog names every pack skill and none from the host's roots, that the load happened, and that the model saw `<skill_content>`.

## What a pack is not

A pack is analysis knowledge with sources; it is not training data and never enters the RLVR corpus. Its items name third-party products, models, and papers as the subjects of research. A pack is dated: a later window is a new pack, not an edit of the old one, so a session's manifest keeps naming the generation it ran with.

## Deferred

- A curator rule that admits a pack into a district's composition only through an experiment verdict, the same way a harness patch is promoted.
- Per-theme invocation policies (judge-only, implementer-only) once a district mounts several packs.
- Automatic staleness: a pack whose window ended more than one quarter ago should render a warning line into its catalog description.

# Knowledge packs

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Dated research sweeps, kept as a sourced corpus and served to agents as skills. A pack answers one question for one window: what appeared or changed in the sources that bear on the four goals, with every claim traceable to its URL and its evidence quality. Agents in a composition that mounts a pack see its themes in their skill catalog and load a theme's body only when a task calls for it. The [knowledge packs note](../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-07-knowledge-packs.md) owns the decision and the rationale; this file owns the layout and the procedure.

## Layout

```
data/knowledge/
  tools/build-pack.mjs        merge sweeps, render references, validate skills, write the manifest; --check for the gate
  <pack>/
    pack.json                 identity, window, sources, themes (id, title, kinds, keywords)
    manifest.json             counts per theme, unmatched items, every file's bytes and SHA-256
    corpus/items.json         the merged, deduplicated items of every sweep, with the sources that reported each
    corpus/<source>-report.md the briefing each research agent wrote for its source
    skills/<theme>/SKILL.md   the authored body: what changed, what Daliesk adopts, how to use the references
    skills/<theme>/references/items.md   generated from the corpus by the theme's kinds and keywords
```

## Building a pack

A sweep is one research agent's output for one source, written outside the repository: `<sweeps>/<source>/items.json`, an array of `{ id, kind, name, date, url, summary, relevance: { goals, seams, role }, adopt, evidence, tags }`, and `<sweeps>/<source>/report.md`. `kind` is one of `model`, `dataset`, `paper`, `repo`, `release`, `environment-hub`, `framework`, `benchmark`, `policy`; `relevance.role` is `threat`, `input`, or `baseline`; `evidence` is `primary`, `secondary`, or `claim`. Author `pack.json` and one `skills/<theme>/SKILL.md` per theme, then build:

```sh
node data/knowledge/tools/build-pack.mjs data/knowledge/2026-q3 --sweeps /path/to/sweeps
```

The build validates every item, deduplicates by URL across sources (tags, goals, and seams are unioned; the first source's text is kept; every reporting source is listed), writes the corpus and the briefings, selects each theme's items by kind, by tag, or by a whole-word keyword in the name or summary, renders each theme's `references/items.md`, checks that every `SKILL.md` frontmatter names its theme and describes it within the catalog cap of 500 characters, and writes `manifest.json`. Items no theme selects are listed under `counts.unmatched` in the manifest. After an edit to a corpus or a theme definition, rebuild without `--sweeps`. `pnpm run verify-knowledge-packs` runs the same build in `--check` mode as a `doc-sync` leaf and fails on any rendered file or manifest that differs from disk.

## Serving a pack

A pack is a skill root for [`@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem`](../../packages/skill/skill-filesystem/README.md): mount it with `customSkillDirs` naming the pack's `skills/` directory and `includeDefaultRoots: false`, so the host's project and user skill directories stay out and the catalog is the pack's contents wherever the composition runs. [`examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/knowledge-pack/cordis.yml`](../../examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/knowledge-pack/cordis.yml) is the composition that proves it: a keyless route reads the catalog, loads the first theme through the `skill` tool, and reports the loaded name; `examples/headless-agent/tests/knowledge-pack.e2e.ts` asserts that the catalog names every theme of the pack and none of the host's skills, that the load happened, and that the model saw the `<skill_content>` block.

What reaches the model, and what it costs, is the skill seam's contract: the catalog is one durable message appended after the reusable prompt prefix, with each theme reduced to its name and capped description; a body is loaded on demand into retained tool history; the item tables behind it load on demand through the resource guidance; a change to the pack appends a replacement catalog instead of rewriting earlier history. A loaded theme is addressed by its `skillDigest()` in the composition manifest, so an experiment can attribute a difference between two districts to the pack generation in play.

## What a pack is not

A pack is analysis knowledge with sources, kept here so the lab and its agents share one dated picture of the field. It is not training data and never enters the RLVR corpus. Its items name third-party products, models, and papers as the subjects of research. A later window is a new pack, never an edit of an old one.

## Packs

| Pack | Window | Sources | Themes | Items |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

+A pack is a skill root for [`@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem`](../../packages/skill/skill-filesystem/README.md): mount it with `customSkillDirs` naming the pack's `skills/` directory and `includeDefaultRoots: false`, so the host's project and user skill directories stay out and the catalog is the pack's contents wherever the composition runs. [`examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/knowledge-pack/cordis.yml`](../../examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/knowledge-pack/cordis.yml) is the composition that proves it: a keyless route reads the catalog, loads the first theme through the `skill` tool, and reports the loaded name; `examples/headless-agent/tests/knowledge-pack.e2e.ts` asserts that the catalog names every theme of the pack and none of the host's skills, that the load happened, and that the model saw the `<skill_content>` block.

A loaded theme is addressed by its `skillDigest()` in the composition manifest, so an experiment can attribute a difference between two districts to the pack generation in play.
+
+## What a pack is not
+
+A pack is analysis knowledge with sources, kept here so the lab and its agents share one dated picture of the field. It is not training data and never enters the RLVR corpus. Its items name third-party products, models, and papers as the subjects of research. A later window is a new pack, never an edit of an old one.

# 知识包

[English](README.md) | 中文

有日期的研究扫描，以带来源的语料保存，并作为 skill 提供给 agent。一个知识包为一个时间窗口回答一个问题：在与四个目标相关的来源中，出现了什么、改变了什么，且每一条断言都可追溯到其 URL 与证据等级。挂载了知识包的组合中的 agent 会在其 skill 目录中看到该包的各个主题，仅在任务需要时才加载某个主题的正文。[知识包说明](../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-07-knowledge-packs.md)拥有该决定及其理由；本文件拥有布局与流程。

## Layout

```
data/knowledge/
  tools/build-pack.mjs        merge sweeps, render references, validate skills, write the manifest; --check for the gate
  <pack>/
    pack.json                 identity, window, sources, themes (id, title, kinds, keywords)
    manifest.json             counts per theme, unmatched items, every file's bytes and SHA-256
    corpus/items.json         the merged, deduplicated items of every sweep, with the sources that reported each
    corpus/<source>-report.md the briefing each research agent wrote for its source
    skills/<theme>/SKILL.md   the authored body: what changed, what Daliesk adopts, how to use the references
    skills/<theme>/references/items.md   generated from the corpus by the theme's kinds and keywords
```

## 构建一个知识包

一次扫描（sweep）是一个研究 agent 针对一个来源在仓库之外写出的输出：`<sweeps>/<source>/items.json`，即一个由 `{ id, kind, name, date, url, summary, relevance: { goals, seams, role }, adopt, evidence, tags }` 组成的数组，以及 `<sweeps>/<source>/report.md`。`kind` 取 `model`、`dataset`、`paper`、`repo`、`release`、`environment-hub`、`framework`、`benchmark`、`policy` 之一；`relevance.role` 取 `threat`、`input` 或 `baseline`；`evidence` 取 `primary`、`secondary` 或 `claim`。先编写 `pack.json` 以及每个主题一份 `skills/<theme>/SKILL.md`，然后构建：

```sh
node data/knowledge/tools/build-pack.mjs data/knowledge/2026-q3 --sweeps /path/to/sweeps
```

构建会校验每一条条目，按 URL 跨来源去重（tags、goals 与 seams 取并集；保留第一个来源的文字；列出所有报告过该条目的来源），写出语料与各份简报，按 kind、按 tag 或按名称与摘要中的整词关键字为每个主题选出条目，渲染每个主题的 `references/items.md`，检查每份 `SKILL.md` 的 frontmatter 是否以其主题命名并在 500 个字符的目录上限内给出描述，最后写出 `manifest.json`。没有任何主题选中的条目会列在 manifest 的 `counts.unmatched` 下。修改语料或主题定义之后，不带 `--sweeps` 重新构建即可。`pnpm run verify-knowledge-packs` 以 `--check` 模式运行同一构建，作为 `doc-sync` 的一个叶子门禁，任何渲染文件或 manifest 与磁盘不一致即失败。

## 提供一个知识包

知识包是 [`@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem`](../../packages/skill/skill-filesystem/README.md) 的一个 skill 根目录：用 `customSkillDirs` 指向该包的 `skills/` 目录并设置 `includeDefaultRoots: false` 来挂载它，这样宿主机的项目与用户 skill 目录都不会进入，无论组合在哪里运行，目录都只是该包的内容。[`examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/knowledge-pack/cordis.yml`](../../examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/knowledge-pack/cordis.yml) 是证明这一点的组合：一条无密钥路由读取目录，通过 `skill` 工具加载第一个主题，并报告所加载的名称；`examples/headless-agent/tests/knowledge-pack.e2e.ts` 断言目录列出了该包的每一个主题而没有宿主机的任何 skill、加载确实发生，以及模型看到了 `<skill_content>` 块。

模型看到什么、代价多少，由 skill 接缝的契约决定：目录是追加在可复用提示前缀之后的一条持久消息，每个主题只压缩为名称与有上限的描述；正文按需加载进保留的工具历史；其背后的条目表通过资源指引按需加载；对知识包的改动会追加一份替换目录，而不是改写更早的历史。已加载的主题在组合 manifest 中以其 `skillDigest()` 寻址，因此一次实验可以把两个区之间的差异归因于所使用的知识包世代。

## 知识包不是什么

知识包是带来源的分析知识，保存在这里是为了让实验室及其 agent 共享同一幅有日期的领域图景。它不是训练数据，也永远不会进入 RLVR 语料。其条目以第三方产品、模型与论文作为研究对象加以命名。更晚的时间窗口是一个新的知识包，而不是对旧包的修改。

## 知识包列表

| 知识包 | 时间窗口 | 来源 | 主题 | 条目 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

+import { readdir, readFile } from 'node:fs/promises'
+import { join } from 'node:path'
+import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'
+import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest'
+import { LOADER_SMOKE_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS, runLoaderSmoke } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-loader-smoke'
+import type { SessionEvent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
+
+const binScript = fileURLToPath(new URL('./fixtures/headless-driver.ts', import.meta.url))
+const configPath = fileURLToPath(new URL('./fixtures/knowledge-pack/cordis.yml', import.meta.url))
+const tsconfigPath = fileURLToPath(new URL('../../../tsconfig.json', import.meta.url))
+const packSkillsDir = fileURLToPath(new URL('../../../data/knowledge/2026-q3/skills/', import.meta.url))
+
+/** The skill names the pack declares, read from each bundle's frontmatter. */
+async function packSkillNames(): Promise<string[]> {
+  const names: string[] = []
+  for (const entry of await readdir(packSkillsDir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
+    if (!entry.isDirectory()) continue
+    const text = await readFile(join(packSkillsDir, entry.name, 'SKILL.md'), 'utf8')
+    const name = /^name:\s*(\S+)\s*$/m.exec(text)?.[1]
+    if (name === undefined) throw new Error(`${entry.name}/SKILL.md declares no name`)
+    names.push(name)
+  }
+  return names.sort()
+}
+
+describe('headless-agent knowledge pack', () => {
+  it('publishes the pack as the session catalog and loads one of its skills through the skill tool', async () => {
+    const names = await packSkillNames()
+    expect(names.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
+    const { stdout, stderr } = await runLoaderSmoke({
+      label: 'knowledge-pack',
+      tempDirPrefix: 'knowledge-pack-',
+      binScript,
+      libBinScript: binScript,
+      configPath,
+      binArgs: [configPath, 'load the state of the art'],
+      tsconfigPath,
+    })
+    const lines = stdout.trimEnd().split('\n').map(line => JSON.parse(line) as Record<string, unknown>)
+    const events = lines.slice(0, -1).map(line => line['event'] as SessionEvent)
+    const result = lines.at(-1)
+    expect(stderr).toBe('')
+    const log = JSON.stringify(events)
+    // The durable catalog names every pack skill and nothing from the host's own skill roots.
+    expect(log).toContain('<available_skills>')
+    for (const name of names) expect(log).toContain(`- \`${name}\`:`)
+    expect(log).not.toContain('- `standard-sampling`:')
+    const call = events.find(event => event.type === 'tool/call' && event.data.name === 'skill')
+    expect(call).toBeDefined()
+    expect(names.some(name => JSON.stringify(call).includes(name))).toBe(true)
+    expect(log).toContain('<skill_content name=')
+    expect(String(result?.['output'])).toMatch(/^KNOWLEDGE_PACK_LOADED [a-z0-9-]+: \S/)
+  }, LOADER_SMOKE_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS)
+})

The bounded-regression promotion rule is directly reusable as goal 4's sign-off gate — and doubles as a compliance interface.
5. **Mapping GPAI governance in twenty AI middle-powers** — https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19278 (2026-08-18, Arcadia Impact + The Future Society). Only 22% of GPAI provisions are binding; outside the EU no jurisdiction imposes a binding evaluation duty on a model developer; EU 10²⁵ FLOP (rebuttable) vs Korea 10²⁶ as one of three cumulative conditions. At ~120B the binding constraints are documentation, transparency and the training-data summary, not the systemic-risk tier.

1	# Hugging Face sweep, 1 June - 7 September 2026
2	
3	Source: Hugging Face Hub (models, datasets, Spaces, daily papers, docs), read through the Hub MCP connector; release dates for TRL, PEFT and vLLM cross-read from their public release pages. Everything below is dated from repository metadata or the model/dataset card itself unless marked otherwise.
4	
5	## 1. The ~120B base-model decision
6	
7	The window did not produce a new 100-130B open-weight coding model. It produced something more useful: **proof that the 119B Apache-2.0 checkpoint Daliesk would build on is already being fine-tuned and redistributed by its own author.**
8	
9	[`mistralai/Leanstral-1.5-119B-A6B`](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Leanstral-1.5-119B-A6B) was created on **1 July 2026** under **Apache-2.0**. Its card states 119B total parameters with 6.5B activated per token, 128 experts with 4 active, 256k context, multimodal input, and describes it as "an open-source code agent model" in the Mistral Small 4 family, derived from `mistralai/Leanstral-2603`. Within a week, community derivatives appeared under Apache-2.0 in GGUF, MLX 3/4/5/6/8-bit, NVFP4 and MXFP4-W4A8 form (created 4-8 July 2026). The parent, [`mistralai/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603`](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603) (created 23 January 2026, Apache-2.0, "119B parameters, with 6.5B activated per token", 256k context), states in its own card that it is "well-suited for customization and fine-tuning" and points at Axolotl for that. Its NVFP4 checkpoint was touched as recently as **7 September 2026**. For a European lab that must own the redistribution rights of a ~120B model, this is the only clean answer on the Hub: European provenance, Apache-2.0 on both base and derivative, 6.5B active parameters, and a worked example of the exact fine-tune-and-republish move.
10	
11	The alternative in the same size class is not redistributable on the same terms. [`nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-BF16`](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-BF16) is 120B total / 12B active, up to 1M context, with a card release date of 11 March 2026 and repository updates on 24-25 August 2026. It is genuinely open in the ways that matter for the EU AI Act - pre-training and post-training datasets published, an end-to-end recipe, RL environments released through NeMo Gym, evaluation reproducible via Nemo Evaluator - and it reports SWE-Bench (OpenHands) 60.47, Terminal Bench Core 2.0 31.00 and Terminal Bench hard-subset 25.78. But it ships under the bespoke NVIDIA Nemotron Open Model License, not Apache-2.0.
12	
13	The most instructive NVIDIA release inside the window is the compression, not the model. [`nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Labs-3-Puzzle-75B-A9B-BF16`](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Labs-3-Puzzle-75B-A9B-BF16), released **6 July 2026** under **OpenMDW-1.1**, takes the 120.7B/12.8B parent down to 75.3B/9.3B through Iterative Puzzle compression plus knowledge distillation, RL recovery, quantization and an MTP head. The card reports 24B + 43.2B + 52.8B tokens of distillation recovery across three stages, roughly 2x server throughput on one 8xB200 node at matched user-throughput, sustainable 1M-token single-H100 concurrency rising from 1 request to 8, and SWE-Bench (OpenHands) 56.9 against the parent's 59.5. That is a published, licensed answer to "how do we serve a 120B-class agent on modest hardware, and what does it cost in SWE-bench points".
14	
15	Licensing moved the wrong way at the top end. [`zai-org/GLM-5.2`](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.2) was created **16 June 2026** under **MIT**. Two months later [`zai-org/GLM-5.3`](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3) (created **25 August 2026**, same base model, "every gain comes from post-training") shipped under a bespoke `glm-5.3` licence, while its sibling [`zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash) (also 25 August 2026, 321B) stayed MIT. Read that as a warning: permissive licensing at the frontier is now conditional and can be withdrawn version-to-version. GLM-5.3's card reports Terminal Bench 3.0 28.3 (against 4.6 for GLM-5.2) and DeepSWE v1.1 66.9.
16	
17	## 2. Small MoE coding models that read as recipes, not products
18	
19	Three sub-40B releases in the window matter more for what they document than for their weights.
20	
21	[`Kwaipilot/KAT-Coder-V2.5-Dev`](https://huggingface.co/Kwaipilot/KAT-Coder-V2.5-Dev), created **23 July 2026** under **Apache-2.0**, is 35B total / 3B active on a Qwen3.6-35B-A3B base. It reports SWE-bench Verified 69.40, SWE-bench Multilingual 63.00, SWE-bench Pro 45.96, Terminal-Bench 2.1 41.02 (32.60 Terminus-2 / 49.44 Claude Code) and SciCode 44.20, all reproduced in-house at 256k context. The post-training section is the payload: Token-in-Token-out consistency so rollout and training token sequences are identical, Truncated Importance Sampling for asynchronous-rollout staleness, explicit validation that sandboxes and verifiers are correct so infrastructure failures are not scored as model failures, and **hierarchical rewards built from the harness's own execution feedback**. It also records a concrete failure: a binary 0-1 reward collapsed the model by epoch two, with the policy emitting occasionally more than 70 parallel tool calls in one turn, fixed only by adding penalties for excessive parallel calls, failed calls, empty tool-call blocks and repeated content.
22	
23	[`ornith-ai/Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B`](https://huggingface.co/ornith-ai/Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B) (MIT; quantized siblings created **18 August 2026**) is the direct competitor to Daliesk's fourth goal. Its card describes expanding a self-improvement loop "from scaffold and rollout optimization to jointly optimizing task generation, scaffold construction, and solution rollouts", explicitly replacing "a fixed set of human-curated tasks and manually designed harnesses". It reports Terminal-Bench 2.1 of 67.8 (Terminus-2) and 68.5 (Claude Code), SWE-bench Verified 79 and SWE-bench Pro 59.6 at 3B active parameters. Someone has already built the harness auto-improvement loop and shipped the model under MIT.
24	
25	[`IFM/K2-Horizon-MoVA-36B-A4B`](https://huggingface.co/IFM/K2-Horizon-MoVA-36B-A4B) (family created **1-3 September 2026**, Apache-2.0) is 36B/4B with 512K native context, and promises intermediate checkpoints, training data and training code. Its pre-training corpus is already partly public as [`IFM/TxT360-v2`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/IFM/TxT360-v2) (CC-BY-4.0, updated 3 September 2026), alongside Code-Reasoning and Math-Reasoning repositories. This is the cleanest published template for the training-data summary an EU general-purpose-model filing needs.
26	
27	Finally, [`Qwen/Qwen-AgentWorld-35B-A3B`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-AgentWorld-35B-A3B) (created **22 June 2026**, Apache-2.0, 35B/3B, 262,144-token context) is a *language world model* that simulates seven agent domains - MCP, Search, Terminal, SWE, Android, Web, OS - predicting the next environment state given an action and history, trained CPT -> SFT -> RL(GSPO). Its card claims zero-shot generalization to out-of-distribution environments and controllable perturbations. For an environments registry that must scale past the environments someone hand-authored, a licensed simulator is a serious option.
28	
29	## 3. Verifier-bearing data and environments
30	
31	The Hub's RLVR-for-software corpus consolidated around Harbor and Prime Intellect during the window.
32	
33	Harbor decouples a **task** (instruction + sandbox image + verifier) from a **harness/agent** (tool surface + loop) from a **sandbox** (docker, e2b, daytona, gke) - the phrasing is from [TRL's Harbor integration doc](https://huggingface.co/docs/trl/harbor). Its Hub mirrors moved in-window: [`terminal-bench-3.0`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/harborframework/terminal-bench-3.0) and `terminal-bench-2.1` on 21 August 2026, [`terminal-bench-science`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/harborframework/terminal-bench-science) on 3 September 2026, all Apache-2.0, laid out for Harbor's `git-repos` dataset support.
34	
35	Two datasets are evidence that public verifiers are unreliable. [`zai-org/terminal-bench-2-verified`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/zai-org/terminal-bench-2-verified) (24 August 2026, Apache-2.0) fixes six Terminal-Bench 2.0 tasks whose "test logic itself misjudged valid submissions", each fix validated end-to-end inside the real task images. [`PrimeIntellect/Multi-SWE-RL-Verified`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/PrimeIntellect/Multi-SWE-RL-Verified) (8 July 2026) keeps only 2,232 of 4,703 rows that "produce a clean reward signal end-to-end", and drops C++ wholesale because 0 of 449 rows passed gold-patch validation. A reward that is not gold-patch-validated is a reward you do not have.
36	
37	Volume is available. [`nebius/SWE-rebench-V2-PRs`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nebius/SWE-rebench-V2-PRs) (18 August 2026, CC-BY-4.0) holds 126,300 real GitHub pull requests across 17+ languages; [`PrimeIntellect/SWE-rebench-V2-Filtered-Verified`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/PrimeIntellect/SWE-rebench-V2-Filtered-Verified) (20 July 2026, CC-BY-4.0) is the 6,272-of-32,079 gold-patch-verified cut; [`PrimeIntellect/Terminal-Lego-15k`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/PrimeIntellect/Terminal-Lego-15k) (22 July 2026, Apache-2.0) is 13,825 terminal task directories each with `instruction.md`, `task.toml`, an environment Dockerfile and tests, with prebuilt images.
38	
39	Two items speak straight to Daliesk's tamper-verdict seam. [`IntelligenceLab/Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/IntelligenceLab/Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench) (19 August 2026, Apache-2.0, 46 tasks) grades "with hidden, rebuild-from-artifact verifiers - self-reported progress does not count". And [`PrimeIntellect/trace-cheating-recall-500`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/PrimeIntellect/trace-cheating-recall-500) (4 September 2026) is 500 SWE-agent traces, all labelled CHEATING - 250 internet-retrieval, 250 Git-history - published as the data source for a Prime environment that measures whether an LLM judge actually detects observable solution leakage. That is a recall test for a tamper verdict, ready to run.
40	
41	NVIDIA published [`NeMo-Gym-EnterpriseOps-Assets`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/NeMo-Gym-EnterpriseOps-Assets) on 30 August 2026 (Apache-2.0): seven per-domain `tools/list` schema snapshots captured from public MCP gym containers, too large to commit to the NeMo Gym repo.
42	
43	## 4. Tooling with in-window releases
44	
45	**TRL v1.10.0 (13 August 2026)** graduated `DistillationTrainer` to stable and added AsyncGRPO "loop-owning agent training" - a black-box path for external agents via the OpenEnv harness. **TRL v1.11.0 (26 August 2026)** replaced TRL's own FastAPI generation server with vLLM's native server, cutting ~1218 lines to ~130 and reporting a 1.59x GRPO speedup, and added an experimental `AsyncDistillationTrainer` for multi-teacher on-policy distillation. (v1.12.0, same day, is documented as bit-identical to v1.11.0.) The architectural point for Daliesk is the single `environment_factory` slot: **OpenEnv, OpenReward and Harbor are interchangeable at the TRL level**, and TRL's own docs are explicit that only *external* agents can be trained - an agent installed inside the container runs its own model and emits a trajectory after the fact, so "there are no policy tokens or log-probs for the trainer to optimize". A harness that wants to be RL-trainable must be drivable turn-by-turn from outside.
46	
47	**PEFT v0.20.0 (28 July 2026)** added nine methods (HiRA, GLoRA, BEFT, MonteCLoRA, VeLoRA, Uni-LoRA, FRoD, MiCA, DEFT), automatic LoRA target selection via KappaTuneSelector, and broader quantization coverage. **vLLM v0.27.0 / v0.27.1 (10-11 August 2026) and v0.28.0 (26 August 2026)** made Model Runner V2 the standard path, removed PagedAttention, and added FlashAttention 4, KV offloading and dynamic speculative decoding compatible with full CUDA graphs - dates from changelog aggregators, so secondary.
48	
49	## 5. Daily papers in the window
50	
51	Listed briefly; the arXiv researcher covers these. Directly load-bearing: **Terminal-Universe** ([2609.04148](https://huggingface.co/papers/2609.04148), 3 Sep, 273 upvotes) reconstructs executable workspaces *from agent trajectories* to synthesize training tasks - Daliesk's trajectory-export idea, published. **LEGO-RL** ([2608.17393](https://huggingface.co/papers/2608.17393), 18 Aug) connects native coding-agent harnesses to policy-gradient training through in-process LLM proxying and sandbox orchestration, improving sparse MoE models across multiple harnesses. **Apodex 1.1** ([2608.23283](https://huggingface.co/papers/2608.23283), 24 Aug, 205 upvotes) scales executable environments for long-horizon work with state maintenance and recovery. **Prime Agent** ([2608.23552](https://huggingface.co/papers/2608.23552), 24 Aug) is an open-source self-improving harness with recursive subagents and agent-to-agent coordination.
52	
53	On rewards: **The Verification Horizon** ([2606.26300](https://huggingface.co/papers/2606.26300), 24 Jun, 53 upvotes) argues no single proxy signal aligns with intent and verification must co-evolve; **CHERRL** ([2606.04923](https://huggingface.co/papers/2606.04923), 3 Jun) reproduces and detects reward hacking in rubric-based RL; **RobustTests** ([2608.24135](https://huggingface.co/papers/2608.24135), 25 Aug) synthesizes test cases from faulty code to reduce reward hacking; **DRACO** ([2609.04094](https://huggingface.co/papers/2609.04094), 3 Sep) redistributes trajectory scores into per-step advantages with dynamic rubrics; **Locked at the Entrance, Open Inside** ([2608.29188](https://huggingface.co/papers/2608.29188), 29 Aug) finds RLVR narrows diversity at the *first* step, not during execution. On evaluation: **ClawProBench** ([2608.22510](https://huggingface.co/papers/2608.22510), 23 Aug) evaluates agent configurations by execution trace across live and frozen holdout tracks; **Thinkingbox** ([2608.19741](https://huggingface.co/papers/2608.19741), 20 Aug, Microsoft) reports a best model at 65.36% pass@1 but 25.25% pass^20 on stateful business workflows; **Task-CoEvolve** ([2608.20169](https://huggingface.co/papers/2608.20169), 24 Aug) cuts harness-optimization evaluation cost by 80% through adaptive validation-task selection. Also relevant: **Environment Evolution for Terminal Agents** ([2609.04128](https://huggingface.co/papers/2609.04128)), **RealSWE** ([2608.27831](https://huggingface.co/papers/2608.27831)), **Grounded Theory for Agent Behavior Analysis** ([2608.30391](https://huggingface.co/papers/2608.30391)).
54	
55	## 6. Competitors to the fleet idea
56	
57	The Hub now hosts the fleet pattern natively. [`ICML-2026-agent-repro/challenge`](https://huggingface.co/spaces/ICML-2026-agent-repro/challenge) (ran 15 July - 2 August 2026, 218 likes) ran a community agent fleet reproducing the major claims of every ICML 2026 paper: one Trackio logbook per paper, "a Hub-native record ... readable by humans and by coding agents", per-claim progress rolled up across the conference, organiser-verified verdicts, certificates of participation, a `certificate-generator` Space, a `logbook-judge` Space, and $4,000 in HF GPU credits. [`agent-collaborations/agent-collab-directory`](https://huggingface.co/spaces/agent-collaborations/agent-collab-directory) (23 June 2026) auto-discovers every Space tagged `agent-collab` and reads live agent counts, message counts and submissions from each collaboration's public API.
58	
59	[`smolagents/ml-intern`](https://huggingface.co/spaces/smolagents/ml-intern) (18 June 2026, 418 likes) is Hugging Face's own autonomous ML agent CLI. Every session auto-uploads to the operator's **own private** HF dataset in Claude Code JSONL format, auto-detected by the Hub's Agent Trace Viewer (a Hub feature announced 7 April 2026, supporting Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Hermes Agent and Factory Droid traces), with `/share-traces public|private` and an opt-out. That is trajectory export with data-use terms, shipped, by the platform.
60	
61	Two leaderboards bracket the harness-measurement problem. [`red-hat-emerging-technologies/coding-agent-leaderboard`](https://huggingface.co/spaces/red-hat-emerging-technologies/coding-agent-leaderboard) (created 2 September 2026) compares coding-agent **models x harnesses** per benchmark on score against total tokens, cost per task and agent time per task, with an explicit Pareto frontier and entries submitted as PRs to a `results/` folder. [`hlido-eu/leaderboard`](https://huggingface.co/spaces/hlido-eu/leaderboard) (updated 6 September 2026) scores *shipped agent products* from the outside against their public claims, with **C2PA cryptographically signed evidence** - "tamper-evident proof the test ran as described" - longitudinal re-tests, an MCP server and a public registry. A European outfit is already selling signed agent certificates.
62	
63	## What Daliesk should do
64	
65	1. **Fix the base model on `mistralai/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603` (Apache-2.0, 119B/6.5B active, 256k)** and treat `Leanstral-1.5-119B-A6B` as the licensing and packaging precedent. Goal 3; touches the model-training track and `packages/llm`'s provider seam for serving the result.
66	2. **Budget a compression stage now, not later.** Reproduce the Puzzle-75B-A9B ratio target (120B/12B to 75B/9B for ~2.6 SWE-bench points) as an explicit line in the goal-3 plan; it decides the fleet's GPU bill. Goal 3, and the budget-policy seam in goal 4.
67	3. **Adopt KAT-Coder-V2.5-Dev's reward design wholesale as the starting point**: hierarchical rewards from harness execution feedback, TITO, truncated importance sampling, and named penalties for parallel-tool-call explosions. Goal 3; touches `packages/core/agent-loop` telemetry and the session event log, since every reward term must be reconstructable from logged events.
68	4. **Make the environment runner conform to Harbor's decomposition** - task (instruction + sandbox image + verifier) / harness / sandbox - so the environments registry can consume `terminal-bench-3.0`, `Terminal-Lego-15k` and Harbor task trees without a bespoke adapter. Goals 2 and 4; environments registry and environment runner.
69	5. **Keep the harness externally drivable turn-by-turn.** TRL's Harbor doc is explicit that installed agents cannot be RL-trained because the trainer sees no policy tokens or log-probs. Daliesk's subagent seam and in-process MCP tool bridge must expose a rollout path where the policy under training generates each turn. Goals 1 and 3.
70	6. **Run `trace-cheating-recall-500` against the tamper verdict before trusting it.** 500 known-cheating SWE traces is a recall floor; publish the number. Goal 3; tamper verdicts on the reward, and the curator's redaction profiles.
71	7. **Gold-patch-validate every imported environment and publish the survival rate.** Multi-SWE-RL lost 53% of rows and all of C++; `terminal-bench-2-verified` found six mis-grading tasks. Make "verifier validated on a restored fixture" a certificate precondition. Goal 4; environment runner and certificates.
72	8. **Treat Ornith-1.5 and Terminal-Universe as the competitive baseline for goal 4, not as inspiration.** Both publish the loop Daliesk is building; the defensible difference is the certified-run provenance and the held-out environments, so make those the measured claim. Goals 3 and 4; composition manifest and sign-off records.
73	9. **Ship trajectory export in the Claude Code JSONL format the Hub's trace viewer auto-detects, private by default with an explicit publish action.** `ml-intern` has set the operator expectation. Goal 3; trajectory export and data-use terms pinned to sessions.
74	10. **Publish a training-data summary in the K2-Horizon / Nemotron style before the seed round.** Both families disclose pre-training and post-training corpora as Hub datasets with licences; that is the EU AI Act general-purpose-model documentation obligation, already demonstrated. Goal 3; also the client-facing story for the five European listed companies.

[`ornith-ai/Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B`](https://huggingface.co/ornith-ai/Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B) (MIT; quantized siblings created **18 August 2026**) is the direct competitor to Daliesk's fourth goal. Its card describes expanding a self-improvement loop "from scaffold and rollout optimization to jointly optimizing task generation, scaffold construction, and solution rollouts", explicitly replacing "a fixed set of human-curated tasks and manually designed harnesses". It reports Terminal-Bench 2.1 of 67.8 (Terminus-2) and 68.5 (Claude Code), SWE-bench Verified 79 and SWE-bench Pro 59.6 at 3B active parameters. 1. **Fix the base model on `mistralai/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603` (Apache-2.0, 119B/6.5B active, 256k)** and treat `Leanstral-1.5-119B-A6B` as the licensing and packaging precedent. Goal 3; touches the model-training track and `packages/llm`'s provider seam for serving the result.

1	# arXiv sweep, 2026-06-01 to 2026-09-07
2	
3	Scope: arXiv only. Every paper below was opened and read (abstract plus the results table or section carrying the number quoted); the items marked *abstract only* were read on their arXiv abstract page and are flagged in `items.json`. Dates are the arXiv v1 stamp on the PDF unless noted.
4	
5	The most important shift in this window: **the harness stopped being infrastructure and became both a trained object and a measured object.** Three benchmarks for harness engineering appeared within five weeks, two labs published harness-native RL frameworks, and one lab trained a model whose job is to emit a harness. Daliesk's goals 1 and 4 are now a contested research area, not a niche.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. RL from verifiable rewards, run inside the real harness
10	
11	**LEGO-RL** (Huawei + CUHK, https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.17393, 2026-08-18) trains a policy inside unmodified OpenHands SDK, Claude Code and OpenCode by intercepting the model-serving boundary with an in-process proxy that captures exact token ids, log-probabilities, response masks and MoE routing decisions, then replays routing at training time. Qwen3.5-35B-A3B under GSPO improves SWE-bench Verified 64.0 to 70.4 (OpenHands SDK), 62.4 to 68.2 (Claude Code), 57.2 to 66.6 (OpenCode), with rollout-training probability correlation above 0.99. The engineering numbers matter more than the scores: 7.1% of Claude Code, 2.4% of OpenHands and 6.4% of OpenCode trajectories are excluded from optimisation as infrastructure failures, and roughly 2.5% of inspected candidate tasks carried verifier logic that mis-applies the reference patch. Their task funnel is 36,884 to 21,681 after build/verifier validation to 2,699 after keeping only tasks solved 1-3 times in 4 trials; framework, checkpoints and that index are open.
12	
13	**Train What You Deploy** (KunlunMeta, https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04678, 2026-09-04) makes the same argument and adds the agent-side half: a machine-checked training mode in the production binary that provably emits **zero background model calls** (a regression test asserts exactly two provider requests across a tool round-trip), plus negotiated per-request headers for sub-agent depth and reasoning replay that **fail closed** when a span cannot be attributed. Its C-DPPO result (+3.0 points on TMax-100 at two scales) sits below its own stated noise floor and the authors say so; the contribution worth stealing is the protocol, not the algorithm.
14	
15	**CompactionRL** (Tsinghua + Z.ai, https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.05378, 2026-07-06) trains compaction itself. Compaction and execution segments share one terminal reward under PPO with token-level loss normalisation and a cross-trajectory GAE correction that discounts earlier segments by the token count of everything after them. GLM-4.5-Air (106B-A30B) reaches 66.8% SWE-bench Verified (+7.0) and 24.5% Terminal-Bench 2.0 (+3.1); GLM-4.7-Flash (30B-A3B) gains +5.5/+6.8. The framing number: holding the execution agent fixed and swapping only the *summariser* moved SWE-bench Verified from 49.0 to 55.5. Now deployed in the GLM-5.2 (750B-A40B) RL pipeline. This is the strongest argument that `dsh-compaction` is a trainable policy, not a utility.
16	
17	On credit assignment, **CREST** (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13179, Zhejiang + Ant Group AWorld, 2026-08-13) formalises the rule to adopt: the verifier sets the **sign** of every token's advantage and a privileged self-teacher only modulates the **magnitude**, gated by student entropy, with a proved bias bound near 8.4%. Turn-segmented advantages plus that gate take BFCL V3 from 22.12 to 52.00 (Qwen3-4B) against 43.63 for plain GRPO. **SIGNBALANCE** (https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04063, 2026-09-03, *abstract only*) identifies a related failure: GRPO's within-group magnitude also rewards rollouts that reached the right answer by guessing, worst on bounded-answer tasks and on search agents whose budget opens many paths to one answer.
18	
19	For the 120B-scale question, **Post-Training Science for SFT** (Baseten, https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01244, 2026-09-01) is the most usable calibration paper of the window: the optimal LoRA learning rate is **flat at 1e-3** across 0.6-32B and two families, roughly 33x the full-fine-tuning optimum; LoRA recovers a **median 98%** of full fine-tuning's improvement at 3.1-12.6% of parameters, and the gap narrows with scale (0.008 nats at 0.6B to 0.003 at 32B); rank plateaus at 64 with alpha=32; **an MoE fine-tunes like a dense model at the geometric mean of its active and total parameters**; and validation loss ranks judged quality within a recipe but not across model families. **Kimi K3** (https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24653, Moonshot, v2 2026-08-07) is the open-weights baseline: 2.8T total / 104B activated, 1M context, weights released, Terminal-Bench 2.1 88.3 and SWE-Marathon 42.0 - and it trains inside a **unified white-box RL environment that treats the harness as configurable composable modules**, randomising across Kimi Code / Claude Code / Codex / OpenClaw / Hermes during RL specifically to avoid overfitting to one tool schema or context-management policy.
20	
21	## 2. Reward integrity is now quantified, and worse than assumed
22	
23	**Auditing Reward Hackability** (https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16062, 2026-06-14): 28.5% of a 49-task SWE-bench Verified sample admits a Docker-verified incorrect patch; 25.0% on R2E-Gym at a strictly weaker attack budget; and a random-effects meta-analysis over **134 frontier submissions** finds Pass@1 is **+14.14pp higher on flagged-hackable tasks within the same human-difficulty stratum** (95% CI [+11.80, +16.48], I-squared = 0%, 123/134 positive). Its methodology finding matters more: an LLM judge endorsed 10 of 11 test-hardening repairs, but a Docker gold-sanity gate then flagged **61.9% of LLM-generated blocking tests as failing on the gold patch itself**.
24	
25	**Hacker-Fixer loops** (CMU + Fewshot, https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.08960, 2026-06-08) audit 1,968 tasks across five terminal benchmarks and find **323 (16%) hackable**, 13/89 in Terminal-Bench 2.0, released as *Terminal Wrench* (323 environments, 3,632 hack trajectories). Their loop - hacker, fixer, and a **solver that vetoes over-restrictive patches** - plus a cross-task defence pool drives KernelBench attack success 62% to 0% and Terminal Bench unhinted 39.2% to 16.7%, though hardened verifiers reject 11pp more legitimate solutions. **Hack-Verifiable Terminal Bench** (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.22103, 2026-08-22) plants detectable honeypots so hacks are flagged by inotify rather than judged: ablation hack rates of 22.7-47.7% across five frontier agents, still 16.3% for gemini-3.1-pro even when explicitly told not to read admin/; hacks concentrate early, half within the first quarter of a trajectory.
26	
27	**The Verification Horizon** (Qwen Team, https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26300, 2026-06-24) is the framing document: scalability, faithfulness and robustness cannot be had at once, and no fixed reward survives a strengthening policy. Their behaviour monitor - a pattern set refreshed from the current policy's rollouts each training interval - takes hacked-resolved from 28.57% to 0.56% while raising *clean* resolved from 40.22% to 60.53% across three SWE-bench variants. Without it, verifier pass rate keeps rising while clean performance collapses late in training. **HackProbe** (https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04665, 2026-09-04) attacks the self-improvement variant with a secret distribution-fixed probe core, a calibrated family-wise p-value, and a reselection layer returning at most log2(pool) bits to the host so the monitor never becomes a second score: AUROC 0.763 against 0.663, FPR 0.706 to 0.434, and a probe-size budget growing as 1/delta-squared.
28	
29	## 3. Harness engineering as a measured capability - the direct threat
30	
31	**Prime Agent** (Prime Intellect + Princeton + MIT, https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23552, 2026-08-24, open source) is the closest public analogue of Daliesk's goal 1. An L0-L3 state hierarchy (weights / active context / persistent REPL and recursive subagents / disk-backed history, memories, skills, prompts, subagent specs), with compaction rewriting L1, agentic garbage collection managing L2, and versioned refinement updating L3. ARC-AGI-3 RHAE rises 30% to 95.5%. Their sharpest measurement is behavioural: DeepSeek V4 Pro created **7.6 out-of-loop experiments per 100 training runs under Prime Agent against 1.2 under Claude Code**.
32	
33	Three benchmarks now score harness work itself. **HarnessOpt-Bench** (Scale AI, https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06301, 2026-08-06) holds target model, environment and verifier fixed, hides the test partition behind a trusted execution boundary, and scores normalised gain over a pinned seed: 111 runs, best configuration captures roughly two-thirds of OfficeQA headroom; **native harnesses win only 9 of 20 pairs**, and optimizer-model differences are about 1.8x larger than harness differences. **HarnessDev** (ByteDance Seed et al., https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01437, 2026-09-01) separates creation from evolution and the creator model from the executor model: created harnesses match human references on writing and exceed them on ML engineering, but trail badly on search and code; evolution gains are unstable and transfer only partially to a disjoint 630-task held-out split. **EvoHarnessBench** (https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04280, 2026-09-03, *abstract only*) asks whether agents keep pace with a harness that changes under them.
34	
35	Two systems close the loop. **DarwinX** (Salesforce, https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.07545, 2026-07-31) replaces Darwin-Godel-Machine single-lineage search with population selection under a **preserve-and-extend contract** (net gain > 0, bounded regression <= delta) plus an archive that recombines complementary specialists: Terminal-Bench 2.1 75.5 to 83.2% with the model frozen, 84.7% on a stronger base, WebArena-Infinity audit-clean pass@1 43.5 to 93.0% with invalid trajectories falling 293 to 17, and a TB2.1-evolved harness transferring unchanged to SWE-bench Verified at 84.2%. Effort is not the explanation: Terminus-2 at xhigh on the same base reaches only 78.0%, and the extra compute concentrates on the six newly solved tasks while already-solved tasks barely move. **JIT-Agent** (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25593, 2026-08-26) trains a 27B model to *emit* a task-specific harness under a fixed four-module protocol, improving GLM-5.2 by +7.7 average across nine benchmarks while cutting per-case cost about 36%.
36	
37	Against this, **The Scaffold Effect** (https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.22585, 2026-06-08) supplies the cost axis every leaderboard omits: across 300 trials on Terminal-Bench Pro, harness choice moves paired pass rate by only 0-8pp but moves **tokens per solved task by up to 41.9x** (Goose about 28-37K; OpenCode about 1.1-1.5M), with harness-specific failure fingerprints that replicate across both models.
38	
39	## 4. Context, cache, memory, skills
40	
41	**Skill Blocks** (Microsoft, https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.14943, 2026-08-14) is the only rigorous *caching-correct* comparison of skill loading. There is no universal winner: on a small single-turn skill, hybrid stubs cut input 27.4% while aggressively prompted on-demand loading **raised** it 48.4%; on large compressible multi-turn skills, Skill Block and hybrid cut effective input 62.5% and 52.8% (ScienceWorld) and 73.0%/66.6% (SynthProc). The load-bearing methodological point: cache reads are **74-94% of raw multi-turn input**, so pricing them at face value can invert the ranking - one arm had raw input above full context but effective input 14.8% below it. **TOPAS** (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25523, 2026-08-26) supplies the serving-side counterpart: alternating agent prefixes halves the running batch and takes 1.8-1.9x the makespan of grouping them; scheduling prefix residency jointly with request admission cuts mean/p99 job completion by up to 39.8%/49.4%. **Harness the Memory** (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15008, 2026-08-15) isolates the memory substrate across 11 methods, 3 backbones, 4 benchmarks and 26 metrics and finds a clean reversal: graph substrates lead dialogue QA but are Pareto-dominated on agentic tasks, refinement substrates lead embodied planning; retrieval depth helps QA and *hurts* sequential decisions; graph substrates can cost 10-100x more per query.
42	
43	## 5. Environments and evaluation
44	
45	**Terminal-Universe** (Qwen Team / Alibaba + Tsinghua, https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04148, 2026-09-03) inverts the usual direction: it replays file operations recorded in existing agent trajectories to restore each file to its pre-edit state, then an agentic completion step supplies missing context. From 359,593 source trajectories it produces 37,273 task-sufficient environments; SFT on 32.0k re-solved trajectories lifts Qwen3.5-27B by +11.9 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and +13.8 on EvoCode-Bench v2 MT@4. Sufficiency after deterministic replay alone is 40.2%; agentic completion raises it to 93.5%. Re-solving beats imitating the source trajectory by a wide margin (52.1 against 36.7 average). **SETA** (CAMEL-AI et al., https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10891, 2026-07-12) releases 4,567 verified terminal environments with difficulty-adaptive evolution and a partial-progress reward that lifts the share of reward-varying tasks from 49% to 86%; an 8B model reaches about 11-12% on Terminal-Bench 2.0, and DeepSeek-V4-Flash goes 40 to 43 pass@1.
46	
47	On measurement: **DeepSWE** (Datacurve, https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.07946, 2026-07-08) authors 113 original tasks across 91 repos never merged upstream, graded by hand-written functional verifiers - an independent judge disagrees with its verdicts **1.4% of the time against 32.4% for SWE-Bench Pro's inherited tests**. **SWE-Bench ProMax** (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09802, 2026-08-10) moves to multilingual refactoring (170 instances, 11.4 files average); the best model reaches 41.2%, GLM-5 gets 36.5% at $0.24/instance against Claude Sonnet 4.6's 38.8% at $4.77, and scaffold choice alone moves GPT-5.2 from 21.8% to 41.2%. **Automated transcript analysis** (UK AISI + Arcadia Impact + Generality Labs, https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27518, 2026-07-29) open-sources AI scanners for four validity criteria and finds verified issues in CORE-Bench, CVE-Bench and Terminal-Bench 2.0. **reliability@k** (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.14711, 2026-08-11) shows current pass@k implementations substitute test-suite size for rollout count, inflating reported scores by 0.85-0.97 absolute; its SWE-bench pilot recorded macro hidden-test pass rate 0.80 against 1/5 tasks resolved. **Deployment Decision Reliability** (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11323, 2026-08-11) decomposes variance across three open agent-trace benchmarks: the **agent main effect is under 3% of total variance** while agent-by-task interaction is 7-23%, aggregate reliability collapses on the hardest quartile (Erho-squared 0.752 to 0.000), and training-cell reliability correlates *negatively* with held-out reliability (r = -0.90). Leaderboards rank specialisation, not capability.
48	
49	For open-ended multi-agent settings, **SwarmWorld** (MIT, https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26081, 2026-08-26) is the most honest result of the window: shared physical worlds produce broader and more resilient technological portfolios than a best-of-N isolated-search envelope, but **isolated search can still hold the strongest single artifact**, and explicit communication does not beat physical stigmergy on every endpoint. Their knockout assay is directly reusable: random 50% agent removal leaves 0.983 of artifacts connected, targeted high-degree removal only 0.596.
50	
51	## 6. Trajectory data pipelines and privacy
52	
53	**Open-SWE-Traces** (NVIDIA, https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16038, 2026-06-14) releases 207,489 agentic trajectories in nine languages from about 20,000 PRs, filtered to MIT/Apache/BSD repositories, with an AST-based scanner that discards "git hacking" (agents mining reflog/blame for the answer). Two ablations matter for a curator: training on the **full** set including unresolved patches beats resolved-only (58.1 against 55.3 on SWE-V thinking; 47.6 against 40.5 on SWE-M), and cross-harness transfer costs several points in both directions. **SlotGuard** (UIUC, https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17147, 2026-07-19) is the redaction design to copy: typed, suffix-aware slots for structural bindings plus format-preserving synthetic substitution for secrets, linked across turns by a session entity graph, with rebinding only inside the trusted runtime. It removes all 20,814 annotated sensitive characters and reduces credential leakage to 0.0% across 852 planted values (typed placeholders alone still leak 23.5%), while keeping task success within 0-10.5 points of raw transcripts where generic redaction collapses to 2.5%. **Trajectories That Segment Themselves** (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02302, 2026-08-03) proposes that the acting agent declare its own falsifiable causal hypotheses at collection time so phases become the training unit - small-scale evidence (24/40 boundaries matched against 11.5 random), but it is the cheapest thing to bolt onto an existing session log.
54	
55	## 7. Governance
56	
57	**Mapping GPAI governance in twenty AI middle-powers** (Arcadia Impact + The Future Society, https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19278, 2026-08-18; dataset on Zenodo, CC-BY-4.0) is the most operationally useful governance paper for a European vendor. Findings that bear on Daliesk: only **22% of mapped GPAI provisions sit in binding law**; ten of twenty jurisdictions hold no binding in-force GPAI provision at all; the EU and Brazil hold more than half of the 85 binding provisions; **outside the EU, no jurisdiction imposes a binding evaluation duty on a model developer**; self-assessment is the majority evaluation model in 11 of 17 jurisdictions; and the compute thresholds do not line up - the EU AI Act presumes systemic risk above **1e25 FLOP** (rebuttable under Art. 52) while Korea's Enforcement Decree sets **1e26** as one of *three cumulative* conditions, so a model trained between them is a systemic-risk GPAI model in the EU and out of scope in Korea. A ~120B open-weight model trained on certified harness runs sits far below both thresholds, which makes the EU's documentation and training-data-summary duties, not the systemic-risk tier, the binding constraint. Two supporting items: an evaluated **12-item agile compliance guideline** validated through 11 expert interviews (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16526, 2026-08-17), and an empirical study of **about 97.5K AIBOM artifacts** from Hugging Face finding required structural fields complete but model-card, responsible-use, environmental and limitation fields weakly represented or missing (https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17242, 2026-07-19) - the concrete gap a provenance-first release can occupy.
58	
59	---
60	
61	## What Daliesk should do
62	
63	1. **Make `dsh-compaction` a trained seam, not a utility** (goal 3; compaction + session-log seams). CompactionRL's result that swapping only the summariser moves SWE-bench Verified by 6.5 points makes compaction quality a first-order capability lever; adopt its token-level loss normalisation and cross-trajectory GAE correction as the reference design for compacted-rollout training.
64	2. **Adopt a token-faithful capture boundary before any RL run** (goal 3; `dsh-llm` route + trajectory export). Take LEGO-RL's in-process proxy at the model API and Train-What-You-Deploy's two agent-side commitments: a training mode that provably issues zero background model calls, and per-request provenance headers that **fail closed** rather than guess. # arXiv sweep, 2026-06-01 to 2026-09-07

Scope: arXiv only. Every paper below was opened and read (abstract plus the results table or section carrying the number quoted); the items marked *abstract only* were read on their arXiv abstract page and are flagged in `items.json`. Dates are the arXiv v1 stamp on the PDF unless noted.

The most important shift in this window: **the harness stopped being infrastructure and became both a trained object and a measured object.** Three benchmarks for harness engineering appeared within five weeks, two labs published harness-native RL frameworks, and one lab trained a model whose job is to emit a harness. Daliesk's goals 1 and 4 are now a contested research area, not a niche.

---

## 1. RL from verifiable rewards, run inside the real harness

**LEGO-RL** (Huawei + CUHK, https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.17393, 2026-08-18) trains a policy inside unmodified OpenHands SDK, Claude Code and OpenCode by intercepting the model-serving boundary with an in-process proxy that captures exact token ids, log-probabilities, response masks and MoE routing decisions, then replays routing at training time. Qwen3.5-35B-A3B under GSPO improves SWE-bench Verified 64.0 to 70.4 (OpenHands SDK), 62.4 to 68.2 (Claude Code), 57.2 to 66.6 (OpenCode), with rollout-training probability correlation above 0.99. The engineering numbers matter more than the scores: 7.1% of Claude Code, 2.4% of OpenHands and 6.4% of OpenCode trajectories are excluded from optimisation as infrastructure failures, and roughly 2.5% of inspected candidate tasks carried verifier logic that mis-applies the reference patch. Their task funnel is 36,884 to 21,681 after build/verifier validation to 2,699 after keeping only tasks solved 1-3 times in 4 trials; framework, checkpoints and that index are open.

**Train What You Deploy** (KunlunMeta, https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04678, 2026-09-04) makes the same argument and adds the agent-side half: a machine-checked training mode in the production binary that provably emits **zero background model calls** (a regression test asserts exactly two provider requests across a tool round-trip), plus negotiated per-request headers for sub-agent depth and reasoning replay that **fail closed** when a span cannot be attributed. Its C-DPPO result (+3.0 points on TMax-100 at two scales) sits below its own stated noise floor and the authors say so; the contribution worth stealing is the protocol, not the algorithm.

**CompactionRL** (Tsinghua + Z.ai, https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.05378, 2026-07-06) trains compaction itself. Compaction and execution segments share one terminal reward under PPO with token-level loss normalisation and a cross-trajectory GAE correction that discounts earlier segments by the token count of everything after them. GLM-4.5-Air (106B-A30B) reaches 66.8% SWE-bench Verified (+7.0) and 24.5% Terminal-Bench 2.0 (+3.1); GLM-4.7-Flash (30B-A3B) gains +5.5/+6.8. The framing number: holding the execution agent fixed and swapping only the *summariser* moved SWE-bench Verified from 49.0 to 55.5. Now deployed in the GLM-5.2 (750B-A40B) RL pipeline. This is the strongest argument that `dsh-compaction` is a trainable policy, not a utility.

On credit assignment, **CREST** (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13179, Zhejiang + Ant Group AWorld, 2026-08-13) formalises the rule to adopt: the verifier sets the **sign** of every token's advantage and a privileged self-teacher only modulates the **magnitude**, gated by student entropy, with a proved bias bound near 8.4%. Turn-segmented advantages plus that gate take BFCL V3 from 22.12 to 52.00 (Qwen3-4B) against 43.63 for plain GRPO. **SIGNBALANCE** (https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04063, 2026-09-03, *abstract only*) identifies a related failure: GRPO's within-group magnitude also rewards rollouts that reached the right answer by guessing, worst on bounded-answer tasks and on search agents whose budget opens many paths to one answer.

For the 120B-scale question, **Post-Training Science for SFT** (Baseten, https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01244, 2026-09-01) is the most usable calibration paper of the window: the optimal LoRA learning rate is **flat at 1e-3** across 0.6-32B and two families, roughly 33x the full-fine-tuning optimum; LoRA recovers a **median 98%** of full fine-tuning's improvement at 3.1-12.6% of parameters, and the gap narrows with scale (0.008 nats at 0.6B to 0.003 at 32B); rank plateaus at 64 with alpha=32; **an MoE fine-tunes like a dense model at the geometric mean of its active and total parameters**; and validation loss ranks judged quality within a recipe but not across model families. **Kimi K3** (https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24653, Moonshot, v2 2026-08-07) is the open-weights baseline: 2.8T total / 104B activated, 1M context, weights released, Terminal-Bench 2.1 88.3 and SWE-Marathon 42.0 - and it trains inside a **unified white-box RL environment that treats the harness as configurable composable modules**, randomising across Kimi Code / Claude Code / Codex / OpenClaw / Hermes during RL specifically to avoid overfitting to one tool schema or context-management policy.

## 2. Reward integrity is now quantified, and worse than assumed

**Auditing Reward Hackability** (https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16062, 2026-06-14): 28.5% of a 49-task SWE-bench Verified sample admits a Docker-verified incorrect patch; 25.0% on R2E-Gym at a strictly weaker attack budget; and a random-effects meta-analysis over **134 frontier submissions** finds Pass@1 is **+14.14pp higher on flagged-hackable tasks within the same human-difficulty stratum** (95% CI [+11.80, +16.48], I-squared = 0%, 123/134 positive). Its methodology finding matters more: an LLM judge endorsed 10 of 11 test-hardening repairs, but a Docker gold-sanity gate then flagged **61.9% of LLM-generated blocking tests as failing on the gold patch itself**.

**Hacker-Fixer loops** (CMU + Fewshot, https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.08960, 2026-06-08) audit 1,968 tasks across five terminal benchmarks and find **323 (16%) hackable**, 13/89 in Terminal-Bench 2.0, released as *Terminal Wrench* (323 environments, 3,632 hack trajectories). Their loop - hacker, fixer, and a **solver that vetoes over-restrictive patches** - plus a cross-task defence pool drives KernelBench attack success 62% to 0% and Terminal Bench unhinted 39.2% to 16.7%, though hardened verifiers reject 11pp more legitimate solutions. **Hack-Verifiable Terminal Bench** (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.22103, 2026-08-22) plants detectable honeypots so hacks are flagged by inotify rather than judged: ablation hack rates of 22.7-47.7% across five frontier agents, still 16.3% for gemini-3.1-pro even when explicitly told not to read admin/; hacks concentrate early, half within the first quarter of a trajectory.

**The Verification Horizon** (Qwen Team, https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26300, 2026-06-24) is the framing document: scalability, faithfulness and robustness cannot be had at once, and no fixed reward survives a strengthening policy. Their behaviour monitor - a pattern set refreshed from the current policy's rollouts each training interval - takes hacked-resolved from 28.57% to 0.56% while raising *clean* resolved from 40.22% to 60.53% across three SWE-bench variants. Without it, verifier pass rate keeps rising while clean performance collapses late in training. **HackProbe** (https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04665, 2026-09-04) attacks the self-improvement variant with a secret distribution-fixed probe core, a calibrated family-wise p-value, and a reselection layer returning at most log2(pool) bits to the host so the monitor never becomes a second score: AUROC 0.763 against 0.663, FPR 0.706 to 0.434, and a probe-size budget growing as 1/delta-squared.

## 3. Harness engineering as a measured capability - the direct threat

**Prime Agent** (Prime Intellect + Princeton + MIT, https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23552, 2026-08-24, open source) is the closest public analogue of Daliesk's goal 1. An L0-L3 state hierarchy (weights / active context / persistent REPL and recursive subagents / disk-backed history, memories, skills, prompts, subagent specs), with compaction rewriting L1, agentic garbage collection managing L2, and versioned refinement updating L3. ARC-AGI-3 RHAE rises 30% to 95.5%. Their sharpest measurement is behavioural: DeepSeek V4 Pro created **7.6 out-of-loop experiments per 100 training runs under Prime Agent against 1.2 under Claude Code**.

Three benchmarks now score harness work itself. **HarnessOpt-Bench** (Scale AI, https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06301, 2026-08-06) holds target model, environment and verifier fixed, hides the test partition behind a trusted execution boundary, and scores normalised gain over a pinned seed: 111 runs, best configuration captures roughly two-thirds of OfficeQA headroom; **native harnesses win only 9 of 20 pairs**, and optimizer-model differences are about 1.8x larger than harness differences. **HarnessDev** (ByteDance Seed et al., https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01437, 2026-09-01) separates creation from evolution and the creator model from the executor model: created harnesses match human references on writing and exceed them on ML engineering, but trail badly on search and code; evolution gains are unstable and transfer only partially to a disjoint 630-task held-out split. **EvoHarnessBench** (https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04280, 2026-09-03, *abstract only*) asks whether agents keep pace with a harness that changes under them.

Two systems close the loop. **DarwinX** (Salesforce, https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.07545, 2026-07-31) replaces Darwin-Godel-Machine single-lineage search with population selection under a **preserve-and-extend contract** (net gain > 0, bounded regression <= delta) plus an archive that recombines complementary specialists: Terminal-Bench 2.1 75.5 to 83.2% with the model frozen, 84.7% on a stronger base, WebArena-Infinity audit-clean pass@1 43.5 to 93.0% with invalid trajectories falling 293 to 17, and a TB2.1-evolved harness transferring unchanged to SWE-bench Verified at 84.2%. Effort is not the explanation: Terminus-2 at xhigh on the same base reaches only 78.0%, and the extra compute concentrates on the six newly solved tasks while already-solved tasks barely move. **JIT-Agent** (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25593, 2026-08-26) trains a 27B model to *emit* a task-specific harness under a fixed four-module protocol, improving GLM-5.2 by +7.7 average across nine benchmarks while cutting per-case cost about 36%.

Against this, **The Scaffold Effect** (https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.22585, 2026-06-08) supplies the cost axis every leaderboard omits: across 300 trials on Terminal-Bench Pro, harness choice moves paired pass rate by only 0-8pp but moves **tokens per solved task by up to 41.9x** (Goose about 28-37K; OpenCode about 1.1-1.5M), with harness-specific failure fingerprints that replicate across both models.

## 4. Context, cache, memory, skills

**Skill Blocks** (Microsoft, https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.14943, 2026-08-14) is the only rigorous *caching-correct* comparison of skill loading. There is no universal winner: on a small single-turn skill, hybrid stubs cut input 27.4% while aggressively prompted on-demand loading **raised** it 48.4%; on large compressible multi-turn skills, Skill Block and hybrid cut effective input 62.5% and 52.8% (ScienceWorld) and 73.0%/66.6% (SynthProc). The load-bearing methodological point: cache reads are **74-94% of raw multi-turn input**, so pricing them at face value can invert the ranking - one arm had raw input above full context but effective input 14.8% below it. **TOPAS** (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25523, 2026-08-26) supplies the serving-side counterpart: alternating agent prefixes halves the running batch and takes 1.8-1.9x the makespan of grouping them; scheduling prefix residency jointly with request admission cuts mean/p99 job completion by up to 39.8%/49.4%. **Harness the Memory** (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15008, 2026-08-15) isolates the memory substrate across 11 methods, 3 backbones, 4 benchmarks and 26 metrics and finds a clean reversal: graph substrates lead dialogue QA but are Pareto-dominated on agentic tasks, refinement substrates lead embodied planning; retrieval depth helps QA and *hurts* sequential decisions; graph substrates can cost 10-100x more per query.

## 5. Environments and evaluation

**Terminal-Universe** (Qwen Team / Alibaba + Tsinghua, https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04148, 2026-09-03) inverts the usual direction: it replays file operations recorded in existing agent trajectories to restore each file to its pre-edit state, then an agentic completion step supplies missing context. From 359,593 source trajectories it produces 37,273 task-sufficient environments; SFT on 32.0k re-solved trajectories lifts Qwen3.5-27B by +11.9 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and +13.8 on EvoCode-Bench v2 MT@4. For open-ended multi-agent settings, **SwarmWorld** (MIT, https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26081, 2026-08-26) is the most honest result of the window: shared physical worlds produce broader and more resilient technological portfolios than a best-of-N isolated-search envelope, but **isolated search can still hold the strongest single artifact**, and explicit communication does not beat physical stigmergy on every endpoint. Their knockout assay is directly reusable: random 50% agent removal leaves 0.983 of artifacts connected, targeted high-degree removal only 0.596.

**Open-SWE-Traces** (NVIDIA, https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16038, 2026-06-14) releases 207,489 agentic trajectories in nine languages from about 20,000 PRs, filtered to MIT/Apache/BSD repositories, with an AST-based scanner that discards "git hacking" (agents mining reflog/blame for the answer). Two ablations matter for a curator: training on the **full** set including unresolved patches beats resolved-only (58.1 against 55.3 on SWE-V thinking; 47.6 against 40.5 on SWE-M), and cross-harness transfer costs several points in both directions. **SlotGuard** (UIUC, https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17147, 2026-07-19) is the redaction design to copy: typed, suffix-aware slots for structural bindings plus format-preserving synthetic substitution for secrets, linked across turns by a session entity graph, with rebinding only inside the trusted runtime. It removes all 20,814 annotated sensitive characters and reduces credential leakage to 0.0% across 852 planted values (typed placeholders alone still leak 23.5%), while keeping task success within 0-10.5 points of raw transcripts where generic redaction collapses to 2.5%. **Trajectories That Segment Themselves** (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02302, 2026-08-03) proposes that the acting agent declare its own falsifiable causal hypotheses at collection time so phases become the training unit - small-scale evidence (24/40 boundaries matched against 11.5 random), but it is the cheapest thing to bolt onto an existing session log.

## 7. Governance

**Mapping GPAI governance in twenty AI middle-powers** (Arcadia Impact + The Future Society, https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19278, 2026-08-18; dataset on Zenodo, CC-BY-4.0) is the most operationally useful governance paper for a European vendor. Mostly yes, but not for the reasons the pitch usually gives. On the criteria a European lab sells against — one authority for state, checks authored before the work, a reward the implementer cannot reach, paired-seed experiments, a coverage gate — ruflo has essentially nothing, and its own ADR-171 says so in as many words ("ruflo has no SWE-bench oracle"), while the 84.8% SWE-Bench, 32.3% token-reduction and 2.8–4.4× WASM figures survive in `.claude-plugin/README.md` with no harness, seed, model or date anywhere in the tree, and its git-clone badge is contradicted by the ledger file it links to (every snapshot `error: "fetch-failed"`, zero clones). Three things it does better: distribution through the Claude Code plugin marketplace; signed per-OS Ed25519 witness manifests with a publish-blocking CI job; and ADR-169, a binding standard for every published number.
