15	import type { RenderedRequest } from './types.ts'
16	
17	/** Tag prefix framing the rendered conversation when no content already uses it. */
18	export const TAG_BASE = 'dsh'
19	
20	/**
21	 * JSON Schema requested through the product's structured-output option. Tool
22	 * arguments stay a JSON string because the seam carries raw JSON arguments
23	 * end-to-end and never re-serializes what the model wrote.
24	 */
25	export const RESPONSE_SCHEMA: Record<string, unknown> = Object.freeze({
26	  type: 'object',
27	  additionalProperties: false,
28	  required: ['content', 'toolCalls'],
29	  properties: {
30	    content: {
31	      type: 'string',
32	      description: 'The reply to show the user. Empty when this turn is tool calls alone.',
33	    },
34	    toolCalls: {
35	      type: 'array',
36	      description: 'Tool calls to run before the next turn, in the order they should run.',
37	      items: {
38	        type: 'object',
39	        additionalProperties: false,
40	        required: ['name', 'arguments'],
41	        properties: {
42	          name: { type: 'string', description: 'A tool name offered in the prompt.' },
43	          arguments: {
44	            type: 'string',
45	            description: 'That call\'s arguments as a JSON object, encoded as a JSON string.',
46	          },
47	        },
48	      },
49	    },
50	  },
51	})
52	
53	/** One rendering pass: the prompt text plus every verbatim string it embedded. */
54	interface RenderPass {
55	  readonly text: string
56	  readonly contents: readonly string[]
57	}
58	
59	/** Collects verbatim strings so a later pass can detect tag-prefix collisions. */
60	class PromptWriter {
61	  private readonly lines: string[] = []
62	  readonly contents: string[] = []
63	
64	  constructor(private readonly ns: string) {}
65	
66	  /** Append one framing line the harness owns. */
67	  structure(line: string): void {
68	    this.lines.push(line)
69	  }
70	
71	  /** Append one verbatim string and record it for collision detection. */
72	  content(text: string): void {
73	    this.contents.push(text)

150	    writer.close('tool-result')
151	  }
152	}
153	
154	/** Write the tool section: what the harness runs, and the schema of each call. */
155	function writeTools(writer: PromptWriter, tools: readonly ToolSchema[]): void {
156	  writer.open('tools')
157	  writer.structure(
158	    'The harness runs these tools, not you. Ask for a call by putting it in `toolCalls`;'
159	    + ' its result arrives in the next request.',
160	  )
161	  for (const tool of tools) {
162	    writer.open('tool', [['name', attributeValue(tool.name)]])
163	    writer.content(tool.description)
164	    writer.structure('Arguments (JSON Schema):')
165	    writer.content(JSON.stringify(tool.parameters))
166	    writer.close('tool')
167	  }
168	  writer.close('tools')
169	}
170	
171	/** Render the whole prompt text under one tag prefix. */
172	function renderPass(options: GenerateOptions, ns: string): RenderPass {
173	  const writer = new PromptWriter(ns)
174	  writer.structure(
175	    `Answer the last turn of the conversation below. Elements tagged \`<${ns}-…>\` are the harness's`
176	    + ' framing; everything between them is the conversation.',
177	  )
178	  const tools = options.tools ?? []
179	  if (tools.length > 0) writeTools(writer, tools)
180	  writer.open('conversation')
181	  for (const message of options.messages) {
182	    assertTextOnly(message)
183	    switch (message.role) {
184	      case 'system':
185	        writer.open('system')
186	        writer.content(flattenText(message.content))
187	        writer.close('system')
188	        break
189	      case 'assistant':
190	        writeAssistant(writer, message)
191	        break
192	      case 'user':
193	        writeUser(writer, message)
194	        break
195	    }
196	  }
197	  writer.close('conversation')
198	  return writer.finish()
199	}
200	
201	/**
202	 * Choose the smallest tag prefix no rendered content already uses, so a
203	 * message that itself contains the framing cannot be read as framing.
204	 * @param contents - every verbatim string the first pass embedded.
205	 * @returns the base prefix, or the first numbered variant free of collisions.
206	 */
207	export function tagNamespace(contents: readonly string[]): string {
208	  let ns = TAG_BASE
209	  for (
210	    let suffix = 2;
211	    contents.some(text => text.includes(`<${ns}`) || text.includes(`</${ns}`));
212	    suffix += 1
213	  ) {
214	    ns = `${TAG_BASE}${suffix}`
215	  }
216	  return ns
217	}
218	
219	/**
220	 * Render one harness request into the product's system prompt and prompt text.
221	 * @param options - the fully assembled harness request.
222	 * @returns the custom system prompt and the single prompt text carrying tools and conversation.
223	 */
224	export function renderRequest(options: GenerateOptions): RenderedRequest {
225	  const first = renderPass(options, TAG_BASE)
226	  const ns = tagNamespace(first.contents)
227	  return {
228	    // An absent harness system prompt still replaces the product's preset: the
229	    // harness owns every standing instruction this route's model reads.
230	    systemPrompt: options.system ?? '',
231	    prompt: ns === TAG_BASE ? first.text : renderPass(options, ns).text,
232	  }
233	}

1	/**
2	 * Derive the working directory a filesystem tool resolves relative paths against: the calling
3	 * agent's per-session workspace (`exec.agent.session.header.cwd`), so each session's
4	 * `read`/`write`/`edit` act on ITS workspace, not the server's launch dir — mirroring how
5	 * `dsh-tool-bash` defaults a bash `workdir` to the session cwd.
6	 * Non-agent calls return `undefined`, leaving the fallback in the provider rather than reading
7	 * `process.cwd()` at the tool boundary.
8	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs/session-cwd
9	 */
10	
11	import type { ToolExecution } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools'
12	import { canonicalPath } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox'
13	
14	const PARENT_PATH_SEGMENT = /(?:^|[\\/])\.\.(?:[\\/]|$)/
15	
16	/**
17	 * The session workspace cwd for this call, or `undefined` when none applies.
18	 * @param exec - the tool-execution context; only its optional `agent` is read.
19	 * @param requestedPath - the path the provider will resolve; parent traversal
20	 *   makes a symlinked cwd's filesystem identity observable.
21	 * @returns the calling agent's session cwd, or undefined for a non-agent caller (the backend then applies its own default).
22	 */
23	export function sessionCwd(exec: ToolExecution, requestedPath: string): string | undefined {
24	  const cwd = exec.agent?.session.header.cwd
25	  if (cwd === undefined || (!PARENT_PATH_SEGMENT.test(cwd) && !PARENT_PATH_SEGMENT.test(requestedPath))) return cwd
26	  return canonicalPath(cwd)
27	}
28	
29	/**
30	 * Resolution options shared by all model-facing filesystem tools.
31	 * @param exec - the tool-execution context supplying session cwd and cancellation.
32	 * @param requestedPath - the path the provider will resolve.
33	 * @param policyWorkspaceRoot - resolved per-call root, when a mutation carries sandbox policy.
34	 * @returns provider resolution options for the current tool call.
35	 */
36	export function sessionResolveOptions(
37	  exec: ToolExecution,
38	  requestedPath: string,
39	  policyWorkspaceRoot?: string,
40	): { cwd?: string; signal?: AbortSignal } {
41	  const cwd = policyWorkspaceRoot ?? sessionCwd(exec, requestedPath)
42	  return {
43	    ...cwd !== undefined ? { cwd } : {},
44	    signal: exec.signal,
45	  }
46	}
47

# The slice: native tool use on the Claude Code LLM route

Package: `packages/llm/llm-claude-code` (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-claude-code`), provider `claude-code`. Today one `generate()` is one stateless Agent SDK `query()` with `tools: []`, the harness tools rendered as prompt text (`<dsh-tools>` in `src/render.ts`), and the answer requested through `outputFormat: json_schema` as `{ content, toolCalls: [{ name, arguments: <JSON string> }] }` (RESPONSE_SCHEMA in render.ts, parsed in `src/response.ts`), under `maxTurns: MAX_TURNS = 2` (`src/adapter.ts`).

## Diagnosis (already established; do not redo it, but read the evidence)

Models trained on native tool use ignore the prompt protocol: on a request that offers tools they emit a native `tool_use` block for a listed name (`bash`), the product answers `No such tool available: bash`, the model tries again, and the two-turn bound ends the query with `error_max_turns`. The SDK then throws `Claude Code returned an error result: Reached maximum number of turns (2)` AFTER yielding the result message, so the adapter's catch classifies it as `TRANSPORT` instead of `MAX_TURNS`. In a real bench cell, 11 of 12 queries failed this way.

Evidence files (read-only):
- Session log of the failing cell: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-deepseek-harness/f53f80cc-1f77-5d02-a862-99d59ffabdce/scratchpad/bench/runs/smoke-1/.sessions/*/environment-*/session.jsonl
- Probe of the current protocol: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-deepseek-harness/f53f80cc-1f77-5d02-a862-99d59ffabdce/scratchpad/bench/diag/probe.mjs with logs A.log B.log C.log (sonnet, 0/3 success), R4.log (maxTurns 4, still fails), H1a/H1b/H1c/H1o.log (an explicit "you have one native tool" instruction makes sonnet and opus deliver, but only on the second turn, one wasted API call each), H1h.log (haiku breaks the JSON-string `arguments` protocol twice and fails).
- Probe of the fix: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-deepseek-harness/f53f80cc-1f77-5d02-a862-99d59ffabdce/scratchpad/bench/diag/probe-mcp.mjs with logs M3.log M4.log (sonnet), Mh2.log (haiku), Mo.log (opus): 4/4 first-message native calls, 5–6 s per query.
- Prompt material the probes use: system.txt, user.txt, tools.json in the same diag directory.

## The design to implement

1. Offer the harness tools to the product as real tools through an in-process MCP server named `dsh` (SDK `createSdkMcpServer`, or an MCP `Server`/`McpServer` instance passed as the `sdk` server config if that lets the tool declare the harness JSON Schema verbatim; prefer verbatim schema over a zod round trip because the schema the model sees must equal the schema the session log recorded in `request/header`; if you must convert, zod 4.4.3 in the tree has `z.fromJSONSchema`, and any schema it cannot convert must fail loud with a coded `LlmError` before the CLI is spawned). The handler of every tool never executes anything: it returns a fixed short text. The harness runs the call after the query ends, as it does for every other provider.
2. Query options: `mcpServers: { dsh: <server> }` only when the request offers tools; `allowedTools` = the prefixed names `mcp__dsh__<name>`; keep `tools: []` (built-in tools off), `permissionMode: 'dontAsk'`, `disallowedTools: ['AskUserQuestion']`, `strictMcpConfig: true`, `settingSources: []`, `persistSession: false`, `includePartialMessages: true` (the idle watchdog needs the partial events). Remove `outputFormat`. `maxTurns` becomes 1: one assistant message per query. Update the MAX_TURNS contract comment accordingly (a message that calls tools ends the query at the product's turn bound, which is this route's normal terminal for a tool-calling reply, not a failure).
3. Rendering: drop the `<dsh-tools>` section and the "put it in toolCalls" instruction; the conversation rendering (system, user, assistant with earlier tool calls, tool results) stays as it is. Adjust the framing sentence if it still mentions the tools section.
4. Answer: derive it from the query's `assistant` messages, in order (the SDK may split one API message into several `assistant` messages, one per block, as the Mo.log and Mh2.log probes show): text blocks joined become `content`; `tool_use` blocks become tool calls, name with the `mcp__dsh__` prefix stripped (accept the bare harness name too, the model sometimes emits it), `arguments` = `JSON.stringify(input)` (the API delivers parsed input; this is the only representation available and is what every provider adapter of this seam does when it assembles arguments). Thinking blocks are ignored. Unknown tool names are a coded malformed-response failure. No assistant message at all is the existing EMPTY_RESPONSE.
5. Result classification: `success` → answer; `error_max_turns` when at least one assistant `tool_use` was seen → answer with finish reason tool-calls (expected terminal); `error_max_turns` with no tool call → MAX_TURNS_CODE; every other error subtype → `resultFailure` as today; `subtype: success` with `is_error: true` carries a product-side API failure text (for example `API Error: Unable to connect to API: Self-signed certificate detected`, see M1.log) and must map to a retryable code (TRANSPORT for connection failures, the seam's existing classifiers for rate limit and context window). Usage comes from the result message; both subtypes carry it.
6. Throw-after-result: the SDK throws after yielding the result (`Claude Code returned an error result: …` or `Claude Code process exited with code 1`, see Mh2.log). When a result was already received, the throw is not the query's outcome: classify the result, not the throw. Keep the existing TRANSPORT / TIMEOUT / ABORTED classification when no result arrived.
7. Dependencies: whatever you import (zod 4, `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`) must be a declared dependency of the package at the version already in the tree; `pnpm run hygiene` (knip, publint, workspace constraints) must pass. Check `packages/subagent/*claude-code*` and the `dsh-mcp-tool-server` package first: the bridge mode already exposes harness tools to the product over MCP and may own a reusable schema/name conversion; reuse it rather than duplicating (the duplication gate `pnpm run duplication` fails on cross-file clones), but do not make the route execute tools.

## Deliverables

- Code in `packages/llm/llm-claude-code/src` (adapter.ts, render.ts, response.ts, types.ts, index.ts exports, invariant.ts if the companion's statement changes).
- Tests: `tests/adapter.spec.ts` (fake SDK as the existing spec does; add: tool-calling answer through the max-turns terminal, text answer through success, throw-after-result tolerated, unknown tool name, no-tools request builds no MCP server, `is_error` success result mapped to a retryable code), `tests/render.spec.ts` (no tools section), `tests/response.spec.ts`, `tests/config.spec.ts` if config changes, `tests/loader-composition.e2e.ts`, and `tests/real-product.e2e.ts` extended with a case that offers a `bash` tool schema and asserts the answer is one tool call with parseable JSON arguments (it self-skips without the product; you have the product, run it and report the output). Per-file 100% coverage: run the coverage command from docs/testing.md scoped to this package.
- Keyless snapshot: if any snapshot fixture drives this route (search `examples/` and `packages/support` for `llm-claude-code`), re-record or update it per docs/testing.md.
- README of the package: the Model Experience section (what the model sees now: native tools under the `mcp__dsh__` prefix, one API turn per step, no JSON-string encoding; the product envelope is still the one model-visible input the log does not hold) and Known Limitations.
- One Agent Note under `.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-07-claude-code-route-native-tools.md` with the format `verify-agent-note-format` enforces (line 1 `# Agent Note: <title>`, line 3 `Status: proposed`, line 5 the language switch line used by sibling notes, sections `## Problem`, `## Proposal`, bespoke sections, `## Alternatives considered`, `## Acceptance criteria`, `## Risks`), plus its `.zh.md` translation and the `.i18n.yaml` recorded with `pnpm run verify-translation-pairing --write <en path>`. Cite the evidence numbers above (0/3 and 11/12 before; 4/4 after; second-turn-only delivery with the prompt fix; haiku's protocol breakage).
- Generated docs: run `pnpm run doc-sync` and fix whatever it reports (catalogs under docs/ may need regeneration through the repo's own scripts, never by hand).

## Validation before you commit

`pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run lint`, the package's unit tests with coverage, `pnpm run duplication`, `pnpm run hygiene`, `pnpm run doc-sync`, the real-product e2e twice, and a final rerun of the fix probe is not needed. Report exactly which commands you ran and their results.

## Commit

One or a few commits on your worktree branch. Commit message body: what changed and why, no model identifiers of any kind in code, docs, or messages. Every commit message ends with these two trailer lines exactly:

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01HEXjzxR7CyMizem5kFAB4C

The lefthook pre-commit hook runs staged lint, pairing, and whitespace checks; fix what it reports rather than bypassing it. Never commit credentials. Report at the end: branch, SHA(s), commands run with results, open questions.

+#!/usr/bin/env node
+/**
+ * Driver: boot the bench composition and run one frozen paired experiment from
+ * a plan file, then publish the observatory page and document, the session
+ * facts, the trajectories, and `status.json` beside the result.
+ *
+ *   experiment-driver.ts <config> <plan.json>
+ *
+ * The plan file holds `{ name, environments?, tier?, domain?, heldOut?,
+ * repetitions, baseline, candidate, seed?, policyVersion? }`. `environments`
+ * lists registered ids; when absent, every environment whose registered
+ * `heldOut` flag equals the plan's `heldOut` (default false) is selected, then
+ * narrowed by `tier` and `domain` read from each definition's detail. An arm is
+ * `{ provider, model, implementer? }`; `implementer` is forwarded when the
+ * experiments service accepts it.
+ */
+
+import { readFile, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises'
+import { boot, resolveConfigPath } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot'
+import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-loader'
+import type { EnvironmentRunImplementer } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environment-runner'
+import { EnvironmentId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments'
+import type { EnvironmentId as EnvironmentIdType } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments/types'
+import type { ExperimentPlan } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-experiments'
+import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-observatory'
+import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-scorekeeper'
+import { jsonlFileSink } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-trajectories'
+
+interface Arm {
+  readonly provider: string
+  readonly model: string
+  readonly implementer?: EnvironmentRunImplementer
+}
+
+interface PlanFile {
+  readonly name: string
+  readonly environments?: readonly string[]
+  readonly tier?: number
+  readonly domain?: string
+  readonly heldOut?: boolean
+  readonly repetitions: number
+  readonly baseline: Arm
+  readonly candidate: Arm
+  readonly seed?: number
+  readonly policyVersion?: string
+}
+
+const [configPath, planPath] = process.argv.slice(2)
+if (configPath === undefined || planPath === undefined) throw new Error('experiment-driver requires <config> <plan.json>')
+const plan = JSON.parse(await readFile(planPath, 'utf8')) as PlanFile
+
+const ctx = await boot('proving-ground-bench', resolveConfigPath(configPath, undefined))
+try {
+  // Loader siblings mount concurrently; the plan freezes against the settled registry.
+  await ctx.get('loader')?.await()
+  const experiments = ctx.get('experiments')
+  const environments = ctx.get('environments')
+  const observatory = ctx.get('observatory')
+  const scorekeeper = ctx.get('scorekeeper')
+  const trajectories = ctx.get('trajectories')
+  if (experiments === undefined || environments === undefined || observatory === undefined
+    || scorekeeper === undefined || trajectories === undefined) {
+    throw new Error('the bench requires the experiments, environments, observatory, scorekeeper, and trajectories services')
+  }
+  const selected: readonly EnvironmentIdType[] = plan.environments === undefined
+    ? environments
+      .list({ heldOut: plan.heldOut ?? false })
+      .filter((definition) => {
+        const detail = definition.detail as { tier?: number; domain?: string }
+        return (plan.tier === undefined || detail.tier === plan.tier) && (plan.domain === undefined || detail.domain === plan.domain)
+      })
+      .map(definition => definition.id)
+    : plan.environments.map(id => EnvironmentId(id))
+  const startedAt = new Date().toISOString()
+  // An arm's optional implementer rides through as the experiments service defines its arm.
+  const request: ExperimentPlan = {
+    environments: selected,
+    repetitions: plan.repetitions,
+    baseline: plan.baseline,
+    candidate: plan.candidate,
+    workspaceRoot: process.cwd(),
+    ...(plan.seed === undefined ? {} : { seed: plan.seed }),
+    ...(plan.policyVersion === undefined ? {} : { policyVersion: plan.policyVersion }),
+    sink: jsonlFileSink('./experiment.jsonl'),
+  }
+  const result = await experiments.run(request)
+  const snapshot = await observatory.snapshot()
+  const page = observatory.render(snapshot, Date.now())
+  await writeFile('observatory.html', page.html)
+  await writeFile('observatory.json', `${JSON.stringify(page.json, null, 2)}\n`)
+  const facts = await scorekeeper.exportFacts({ sink: jsonlFileSink('./facts.jsonl') })
+  const exported = await trajectories.export({ sink: jsonlFileSink('./trajectories.jsonl') })
+  const status = { type: 'result', plan: plan.name, environments: selected, startedAt, endedAt: new Date().toISOString(), result, rows: page.json.rows, facts, exported }
+  await writeFile('status.json', `${JSON.stringify(status, null, 2)}\n`)
+  process.stdout.write(`${JSON.stringify(status)}\n`)
+} finally {
+  await ctx.fiber.dispose()
+}

# Proving Ground runs

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Records of real Proving Ground runs: the district's certified measurements of one implementer on registered environments, kept exactly as the harness folded and exported them. A run directory is the output of one fleet plan: the cell session logs, the exported session facts, the curator-gated trajectory export, the observatory snapshot and page, the driver's report, and a manifest with every file'

## Layout

```
data/proving-ground/
  <date>-<implementer>-run-<n>/
    manifest.json        repository head, composition, implementer, session ids, per-file bytes and SHA-256
    result.json          the driver's report: fleet report, delegation records, export reports, observatory document
    facts.jsonl          scorekeeper facts, one per cell session
    trajectories.jsonl   curator-gated trajectory export, one per exported session
    observatory.json     the observatory snapshot the page was rendered from
    observatory.html     the rendered observatory page
    sessions/            the cell session logs, one JSONL file per cell, named by session id
```

## Running one

A run is a Loader-booted composition under `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/` driven from an empty directory outside the repository; the driver creates the session store there and writes the exports next to it. The first run used the composition below, with the host's own Claude Code installation and account as the implementer of every cell:

```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/proving-ground-run && cd /tmp/proving-ground-run
REPO=/path/to/deepseek-harness
TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH=$REPO/tsconfig.json node --import $REPO/node_modules/tsx/dist/esm/index.mjs $REPO/examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/village-claude-implementer/driver.ts $REPO/examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/village-claude-implementer/cordis.yml > stdout.jsonl
```

Then record it, which copies the exports, every session log, and the driver's result into a new run directory, writes its `manifest.json` with the repository head, the composition, the implementers read from the run stamps, and every file's digest, and refuses to overwrite a recorded run; add a row below afterwards:

```sh
node data/proving-ground/tools/record-run.mjs /tmp/proving-ground-run 2026-09-06-claude-code-run-2 --composition examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/village-live/cordis.yml
```

A live district (`examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/village-live/`) is recorded the same way from the directory its driver runs in, one slot per run directory: the shift ledger session lands beside the cell sessions and `result.json` holds the driver's status.

A delegated cell's certificate proves that the runner authored the standard before any work started, restored the immutable paths from the fixture over the tree the external agent left, found the check-owned set unchanged, and ran the checks itself. # The slice: an external implementer runs the model the cell names

## Problem (established, do not redo)

The environment runner (`packages/improvement/environment-runner/src/index.ts`, method `delegate`, around line 1020) starts an out-of-process implementer through `implementer.subagents.start(provider, { prompt, parent, signal, label? })` and records `environment/delegation { attempt, provider, runId, stopReason, structured?, usage? }`. The cell's model (`request.model`, e.g. `{ provider: 'claude-code', model: 'sonnet' }`, stamped on `environment/run` and shown on every observatory row and scorekeeper fact) is not forwarded: the Claude Code subagent provider (`packages/subagent/subagent-claude-code`) spawns the product with no `--model`, so every delegated cell runs the installation's default model while its facts claim the arm's model. A fleet plan `{ models: [{ provider: 'claude-code', model: 'sonnet' }], implementer: { kind: 'subagent', provider: 'claude-code' } }` therefore produces mislabeled measurements, and a paired experiment whose candidate arm names a subagent implementer cannot compare like with like. Evidence: a running fleet's product processes show `claude --output-format stream-json … --permission-mode acceptEdits --no-session-persistence` with no model flag (`pgrep -af claude`), and no cell session log holds the product model anywhere.

## Design

1. The subagent seam's start request (`packages/subagent/subagent/src/types.ts`, the options `start(provider, …)` takes) gains an optional `model?: string`: the provider-specific model identifier the child must run. Document it at the Service Definition as the seam's contract: a provider that receives a `model` it cannot honor rejects the start with a coded error (name it in the seam's error taxonomy, e.g. `SUBAGENT_MODEL_UNSUPPORTED`); a provider never silently runs another model.
2. `packages/subagent/subagent-claude-code`: forward `model` to the product (the SDK `model` option / `--model` flag, whichever this provider uses; look at `src/run.ts`, `src/process.ts`, `src/index.ts`, `src/types.ts`), in both its plain mode and its bridge mode. Record the model the child reports in its `system`/`init` message (field `model`, e.g. a full product model id) on whatever this provider already records per run so the parent can log it; if the provider records nothing per run today, expose it on the run result (`result.structured` is model output, do not overload it; add a typed field such as `result.model` or `run.reportedModel`, whichever fits the seam's existing result type; check how the program department's delegation records the same facts so the two stay symmetrical).
3. Other providers (`subagent-codex`, `subagent-acp`, `subagent-dsh-sdk`, the in-process providers): forward when the provider has an equivalent (Codex has a model flag; ACP may not), otherwise reject a start that carries `model` with the coded error. In-process providers that run on the harness's own LLM seam may honor it by selecting the named model on their child session's route if that is a one-line matter, otherwise reject; do what the seam's existing code makes natural, and document each provider's answer in its README.
4. The runner's `delegate()` forwards `model: request.model.model` for a subagent implementer and records on `environment/delegation` both the requested `model` (the cell's `{ provider, model }` is already on `environment/run`, so record only what is new: the model the child reported, as `reportedModel?: string`). Extend the event's JSDoc (`@mode`, `@param` for each payload field) and every invariant, projection, scorekeeper fact, trajectory record, or observatory column that folds delegation records if one of them should surface the reported model (at minimum the scorekeeper fact of a delegated session should be able to tell "requested sonnet, child reported claude-sonnet-…"; keep the change minimal but truthful). Adding an optional field to an existing event payload is additive; do not bump `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` unless the repository's session-log version mechanism note says an additive optional field requires it (read `.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-10-session-log-version-mechanism.md`).
5. The program ledger (`packages/improvement/program`) delegates departments to external implementers the same way (`program/delegation`); apply the same forwarding there if its department spec names a model, otherwise leave a one-line Known Limitation.
6. The bench composition `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/proving-ground-bench/cordis.yml` and its drivers need no change if the plan's `models[].model` values (`opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku`) are aliases the product accepts; confirm by reading the `llm-claude-code` catalog in that file (`productModel` aliases) and state in the runner README that a fleet naming a subagent implementer must name models the provider accepts verbatim.

## Deliverables

- Code and tests in the touched packages with per-file 100% coverage (`pnpm run test:coverage` scoped as docs/testing.md describes); the subagent-claude-code package has keyless tests with a fake product process and real-product e2e tests that self-skip without the `claude` CLI: extend both (the `claude` CLI on PATH is authenticated, run the real ones and report). Add a runner unit test asserting the forwarded `model` and the recorded `reportedModel`, and a loader-booted e2e assertion where the existing external-implementer fixture already runs (search `examples/` for `environment/delegation`).
- Keyless snapshot: if any snapshot transcript shows `environment/delegation`, re-record it per docs/testing.md.
- READMEs: subagent seam (the new request field and the rejection contract), each provider, environment runner (delegation record fields), scorekeeper/observatory if touched.
- One Agent Note `.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-07-delegated-implementer-model.md` in the enforced format (line 1 `# Agent Note: <title>`, line 3 `Status: proposed`, line 5 the language switch line sibling notes use, sections `## Problem`, `## Proposal`, bespoke sections, `## Alternatives considered`, `## Acceptance criteria`, `## Risks`), with its `.zh.md` translation and `.i18n.yaml` recorded by `pnpm run verify-translation-pairing --write <en path>`.
- `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run duplication`, `pnpm run hygiene`, `pnpm run doc-sync` all green; report exactly which commands you ran and their results.

## Commit

Commit on the worktree branch. No model identifiers of the assistant in code, docs, or commit messages (product model aliases such as `sonnet` that already appear in the repository are fine). Every commit message ends with exactly these two trailer lines:

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01HEXjzxR7CyMizem5kFAB4C

content.text:
**Status.** The bench smoke's failure is fully diagnosed and the fix is being built; the subscription is busy in the meantime.

**What was wrong with the harness-loop arm**
- The Claude Code LLM route described harness tools as prompt text and asked for tool calls inside a structured reply. Sonnet, opus and haiku all ignore that and emit a native `tool_use` for `bash` instead. The product answers "No such tool available", the model tries again, and the query dies at the two-turn bound. That is 11 of 12 queries in the smoke and 0 of 3 in isolated probes. An explicit instruction only helps on the second turn, wasting one API call per step, and haiku still breaks the JSON-string argument protocol.
- The fix is proven by a probe: the harness tools offered as real in-process MCP tools with capture-only handlers, one assistant message per query, no structured output. Sonnet twice, haiku and opus all made a native call on their first message, in 5 to 6 seconds per query.
- Two smaller defects also surfaced: the bench composition had no filesystem tools, and the model was never told the workspace is its working directory. Both are fixed and pushed.

**Landed and pushed** (commit `128e037bb`): all thirty bench tasks admitted, the composition fix, the bench end-to-end test, and the bilingual hypothesis-program note. Every doc-sync gate passed.

**Running now**
- Two opus agents in worktrees: the native-tool-use rewrite of the route, and a slice that forwards the cell's model to external implementers. Without the second one, product-loop cells silently ran the installation default. I measured that default as sonnet, so the current fleets are labelled honestly.
- Two product-loop fleets on the subscription over tier 2 and tier 3 tasks, two repetitions each, plus the district on its cadence. The first two tier-2 cells already certified.
- The roles-matrix agent is still on its later roles.

**Next**: merge the two slices, rerun the one-cell smoke until it certifies, then start E0 calibration and the harness-loop versus product-loop experiment on the same cells, and record every run under `data/proving-ground`.

content.subject: Adapters: tools, skills, LLM providers, prompt sections
content.description: New packages under packages/components/: components-tools (tool kind via tools/change + schemas()), components-skills (skill kind via skills/change + list()), components-llm (model-provider kind via llm/adapters-updated + listProviders()), components-prompt (prompt-section kind via system-prompt/change). Each: src/index.ts, src/invariant.ts, tests at 100%, README triplet, group README row, tsconfig/host refs, allowlist entries.
content.activeForm: Building the tools, skills, LLM, and prompt-section adapters

content.subject: Adapters: plugins (loader entries) and preset compositions
content.description: components-plugins: mirror ctx.loader.entries() as `plugin` components following loader/entry-init and loader/partial-dispose; components-presets: mirror ctx.agentPresets.list() as `composition` components whose members are the preset's rows (plugin components read from the composition file), invoke starts a subagent from the preset when the subagent tool supports it.
content.activeForm: Building the plugin and preset composition adapters

content.subject: component_invoke tool
content.description: tool-component-invoke: model-facing tool that resolves a component id, merges its fixed invoke arguments with model arguments, and dispatches through ctx.tools.execute as a nested sub-dispatch (parent token, rootCallId) so approval, guards, and logging apply; refuses components without an invoke route; prompt section documenting the uniform call.

content.subject: MCP server and Ralph workflow producers
content.description: mcp-client registers an `mcp-server` component (members = its current tool generation) under optional components injection; tool-ralph registers its fixed script as a `workflow` component. Update READMEs and notes.
content.activeForm: Adding MCP server and workflow producers

content.subject: Loader-booted e2e and keyless snapshot for the component inventory
content.description: Fixture composition under examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/components-domain mounting registry + adapters + /components + component_invoke; e2e proves inventory across kinds and a component_invoke dispatch through the real tool runtime; snapshot scenario if the harness supports a keyless one.
content.activeForm: Proving the component inventory in the assembled application

content.subject: Phase 3: promotion path (synthesized provenance, certificates as evidence, catalog gate)
content.description: Certificates record components in play; a promotion domain (session events) with lineage; a catalog admission that refuses a synthesized component lacking certificates and approval; tool-cordis dynamic packages register with synthesized provenance; test proving refusal.

content.subject: Docs: update component-registry note, blueprint artifact, commit and push each slice
content.description: Keep the 2026-09-01 note's rollout current, add ledger lines to the Daliesk blueprint artifact, run gates (lint, typecheck, coverage for touched packages, doc-sync), commit per slice with attribution, push to claude/coding-agent-harness-u9l4gt.

content.subject: Landscape report: best harness/agents per category with prices (artifact + summary)
content.description: Consolidate the six research agents' findings into a published report (harness improvement, hundreds-of-agents workflow management, papers-to-workflows, OSS repo search, computer use, base model + RLVR stack + compute + EU AI Act), with pricing tables, ranked shortlists, cost models, and what Daliesk reverse-engineers from each. Link from the blueprint.

content.subject: Base-model decision for the 120B RLVR model
content.description: Present a decision matrix (license fit for an EU commercial product, agentic-coding capability, base-checkpoint availability, cost per step, RL ecosystem, sovereignty optics) with a recommended primary and fallback, then ask the user to decide; record the decision in an Agent Note once made.

content.subject: Design note: trajectory export and environment registry (improvement seam phase 1)
content.description: Bilingual Agent Note under .agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-trajectory-export-and-environment-registry.md: trajectories as a pure fold of the session log (messages, tool calls, results, rewards from certificates and goal completion, provenance: preset, model, components, isolation), JSONL export contract with prior art (verifiers Trace/Task, SWE-smith trajectories, OpenAI chat format), environment registry Service Definition (tasks + completion-standard checks + held-out flag), acceptance criteria, rollout.
content.activeForm: Writing the trajectory export design note

content.subject: Package: dsh-trajectories (fold + exporter service)
content.description: packages/improvement/trajectories: pure foldTrajectory(events, meta) → Trajectory; TrajectoryService at ctx.trajectories with export({ sessions, sink }) reading ctx.sessionPersistence.inspect; JSONL writer; invariant companion; tests at 100%; README triplet; e2e over the verification-domain fixture proving an exported trajectory carries the certificate as reward.

content.subject: Package: dsh-environments (environment registry Service Definition)
content.description: packages/improvement/environments: EnvironmentDefinition (branded EnvironmentId, kind via merge-extensible map, task prompt, fixture, checks in the completion-standard vocabulary, heldOut, owner, provenance), register() returns disposer, list/get; invariant companion; tests; README triplet; group README + index rows + tsconfig/allowlist registrations.

content.subject: Fix agent-provider invoke pointer in dsh-components-subagents
content.description: The adapter advertises `invoke: { tool: 'subagent', arguments: { provider } }`, but the tool-subagent tool takes only description/prompt/run_in_background and is mounted per provider under a configurable toolName. Drop the invoke pointer (the subagent seam cannot see which tool instance is bound to a provider), update JSDoc, README (+zh, re-pair), the 2026-09-01 component-registry note (+zh, re-pair), and both specs; record the gap under Known Limitations.

content.subject: Design note: environment runner (improvement seam phase 2)
content.description: Proposed note 2026-09-05-environment-runner (+zh, i18n): a fresh agent per run rooted at the workspace, goal + standard authored from the environment's checks, the runner as validator executing checks through ctx.shell, attempt loop with directives, declared isolation, report, and the trajectory link.

content.subject: Package: dsh-environment-runner (ctx.environmentRuns)
content.description: packages/improvement/environment-runner: Config {isolation (required), maxAttempts, evidenceMaxChars, checkTimeoutMs?}, run(request) creating an agent via ctx.agents.create with agentDefaultModel selection, goal create+disarm, standard author, followup/whenIdle, check execution via ctx.shell, recordRun/issueDirective/complete, flush, dispose, report; unit tests at 100% with stubbed services; README (+zh); invariant companion.

content.subject: Loader-booted e2e: environment-run fixture and trajectory reward
content.description: examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/environment-run/{cordis.yml,register-environments.ts,driver.ts}: two environments (passing check, failing check), runner with maxAttempts 2, export rewarded trajectories; e2e asserts both reports and the exported reward; register packages in examples/package.json, knip, tsconfig.

content.subject: Docs gates and push for the environment runner
content.description: Update docs/subsystems/improvement.md (+zh) with the runner, SERVICE_PAGE/SERVICE_ROLES/type-link exemptions, model-experience allowlist, regenerate catalogs and graphs (mirror zh graph docs), pairing records, doc-sync, typecheck, lint, knip; commit and push.

content.subject: Judge council review of the workflow draft (7 judge subagents, parallel)

# Proving Ground runs

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Records of real Proving Ground runs: the district's certified measurements of one implementer on registered environments, kept exactly as the harness folded and exported them. A run directory is the output of one fleet plan: the cell session logs, the exported session facts, the curator-gated trajectory export, the observatory snapshot and page, the driver's report, and a manifest with every file's digest. Nothing in a run directory is edited after the run; the table below is read from those files.

## Layout

```
data/proving-ground/
  <date>-<implementer>-run-<n>/
    manifest.json        repository head, composition, implementer, session ids, per-file bytes and SHA-256
    result.json          the driver's report: fleet report, delegation records, export reports, observatory document
    facts.jsonl          scorekeeper facts, one per cell session
    trajectories.jsonl   curator-gated trajectory export, one per exported session
    observatory.json     the observatory snapshot the page was rendered from
    observatory.html     the rendered observatory page
    sessions/            the cell session logs, one JSONL file per cell, named by session id
```

## Running one

A run is a Loader-booted composition under `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/` driven from an empty directory outside the repository; the driver creates the session store there and writes the exports next to it. The first run used the composition below, with the host's own Claude Code installation and account as the implementer of every cell:

```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/proving-ground-run && cd /tmp/proving-ground-run
REPO=/path/to/deepseek-harness
TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH=$REPO/tsconfig.json node --import $REPO/node_modules/tsx/dist/esm/index.mjs $REPO/examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/village-claude-implementer/driver.ts $REPO/examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/village-claude-implementer/cordis.yml > stdout.jsonl
```

Then record it, which copies the exports, every session log, and the driver's result into a new run directory, writes its `manifest.json` with the repository head, the composition, the implementers read from the run stamps, and every file's digest, and refuses to overwrite a recorded run; add a row below afterwards:

```sh
node data/proving-ground/tools/record-run.mjs /tmp/proving-ground-run 2026-09-06-claude-code-run-2 --composition examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/village-live/cordis.yml
```

A live district (`examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/village-live/`) is recorded the same way from the directory its driver runs in, one slot per run directory: the shift ledger session lands beside the cell sessions and `result.json` holds the driver's status.

## What a row proves

A delegated cell's certificate proves that the runner authored the standard before any work started, restored the immutable paths from the fixture over the tree the external agent left, found the check-owned set unchanged, and ran the checks itself. It proves nothing about how the work was done: the external agent's prompts, tool calls, and reasoning stay in its own product, so the cell session holds the stamp, the standard, the delegation records, the runs, and the certificate, and no assistant turn. The exported trajectory therefore carries no step. It is a measurement, not training data, and the `implementer` field on the stamp is what a curated export filters on. The [external implementer note](../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-06-external-implementer.md) owns these rules.

# Proving Ground 运行记录

[English](README.md) | 中文

真实 Proving Ground 运行的记录：该区对一个实现者（implementer）在已注册环境上的经认证测量，完全按 harness 折叠和导出的原样保存。一个运行目录就是一次 fleet 计划的输出：cell 会话日志、导出的会话事实、经 curator 把关的 trajectory 导出、observatory 快照与页面、驱动器的报告，以及带有每个文件摘要的 manifest。运行目录中的任何内容在运行之后都不再编辑；下表由这些文件读出。

## Layout

```
data/proving-ground/
  <date>-<implementer>-run-<n>/
    manifest.json        repository head, composition, implementer, session ids, per-file bytes and SHA-256
    result.json          the driver's report: fleet report, delegation records, export reports, observatory document
    facts.jsonl          scorekeeper facts, one per cell session
    trajectories.jsonl   curator-gated trajectory export, one per exported session
    observatory.json     the observatory snapshot the page was rendered from
    observatory.html     the rendered observatory page
    sessions/            the cell session logs, one JSONL file per cell, named by session id
```

## 运行一次

一次运行是 `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/` 下的一个由 Loader 启动的组合，从仓库之外的一个空目录驱动；驱动器在那里创建会话存储，并把导出写在它旁边。第一次运行使用了下面的组合，以宿主机自己的 Claude Code 安装和账户作为每个 cell 的实现者：

```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/proving-ground-run && cd /tmp/proving-ground-run
REPO=/path/to/deepseek-harness
TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH=$REPO/tsconfig.json node --import $REPO/node_modules/tsx/dist/esm/index.mjs $REPO/examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/village-claude-implementer/driver.ts $REPO/examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/village-claude-implementer/cordis.yml > stdout.jsonl
```

然后记录它：该工具把导出、每份会话日志和驱动器的结果复制到一个新的运行目录，写出带有仓库 head、组合、从运行 stamp 读出的实现者以及每个文件摘要的 `manifest.json`，并拒绝覆盖已记录的运行；之后再在下表中加一行：

```sh
node data/proving-ground/tools/record-run.mjs /tmp/proving-ground-run 2026-09-06-claude-code-run-2 --composition examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/village-live/cordis.yml
```

实时区（`examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/village-live/`）以同样方式从其驱动器运行所在的目录记录，每个时槽一个运行目录：班次账本会话与 cell 会话并排落地，`result.json` 保存驱动器的状态。

## 一行证明了什么

一个被委托的 cell 的证书证明：runner 在任何工作开始之前就编写了标准，在外部 agent 留下的目录树上从 fixture 恢复了不可变路径，确认由检查拥有的文件集未被改动，并亲自运行了检查。它不证明工作是如何完成的：外部 agent 的提示、工具调用和推理都留在它自己的产品里，因此 cell 会话只保存 stamp、标准、委托记录、运行和证书，而没有任何助手轮次。导出的 trajectory 因此不含任何步骤。它是一次测量，而不是训练数据，stamp 上的 `implementer` 字段就是经策展的导出所要过滤的依据。[外部实现者说明](../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-06-external-implementer.md)拥有这些规则。

+# Proving Ground 运行记录
+
+[English](README.md) | 中文
+
+真实 Proving Ground 运行的记录：该区对一个实现者（implementer）在已注册环境上的经认证测量，完全按 harness 折叠和导出的原样保存。一个运行目录就是一次 fleet 计划的输出：cell 会话日志、导出的会话事实、经 curator 把关的 trajectory 导出、observatory 快照与页面、驱动器的报告，以及带有每个文件摘要的 manifest。运行目录中的任何内容在运行之后都不再编辑；下表由这些文件读出。
+
+## Layout
+
+```
+data/proving-ground/
+  <date>-<implementer>-run-<n>/
+    manifest.json        repository head, composition, implementer, session ids, per-file bytes and SHA-256
+    result.json          the driver's report: fleet report, delegation records, export reports, observatory document
+    facts.jsonl          scorekeeper facts, one per cell session
+    trajectories.jsonl   curator-gated trajectory export, one per exported session
+    observatory.json     the observatory snapshot the page was rendered from
+    observatory.html     the rendered observatory page
+    sessions/            the cell session logs, one JSONL file per cell, named by session id
+```
+
+## 运行一次
+
+一次运行是 `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/` 下的一个由 Loader 启动的组合，从仓库之外的一个空目录驱动；驱动器在那里创建会话存储，并把导出写在它旁边。第一次运行使用了下面的组合，以宿主机自己的 Claude Code 安装和账户作为每个 cell 的实现者：
+
+```sh
+mkdir -p /tmp/proving-ground-run && cd /tmp/proving-ground-run
+REPO=/path/to/deepseek-harness
+TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH=$REPO/tsconfig.json node --import $REPO/node_modules/tsx/dist/esm/index.mjs $REPO/examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/village-claude-implementer/driver.ts $REPO/examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/village-claude-implementer/cordis.yml > stdout.jsonl
+```
+
+然后记录它：该工具把导出、每份会话日志和驱动器的结果复制到一个新的运行目录，写出带有仓库 head、组合、从运行 stamp 读出的实现者以及每个文件摘要的 `manifest.json`，并拒绝覆盖已记录的运行；之后再在下表中加一行：
+
+```sh
+node data/proving-ground/tools/record-run.mjs /tmp/proving-ground-run 2026-09-06-claude-code-run-2 --composition examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/village-live/cordis.yml
+```
+
+实时区（`examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/village-live/`）以同样方式从其驱动器运行所在的目录记录，每个时槽一个运行目录：班次账本会话与 cell 会话并排落地，`result.json` 保存驱动器的状态。
+
+## 一行证明了什么
+
+一个被委托的 cell 的证书证明：runner 在任何工作开始之前就编写了标准，在外部 agent 留下的目录树上从 fixture 恢复了不可变路径，确认由检查拥有的文件集未被改动，并亲自运行了检查。它不证明工作是如何完成的：外部 agent 的提示、工具调用和推理都留在它自己的产品里，因此 cell 会话只保存 stamp、标准、委托记录、运行和证书，而没有任何助手轮次。导出的 trajectory 因此不含任何步骤。它是一次测量，而不是训练数据，stamp 上的 `implementer` 字段就是经策展的导出所要过滤的依据。[外部实现者说明](../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-06-external-implementer.md)拥有这些规则。

# Proving Ground runs

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Records of real Proving Ground runs: the district's certified measurements of one implementer on registered environments, kept exactly as the harness folded and exported them. A run directory is the output of one fleet plan: the cell session logs, the exported session facts, the curator-gated trajectory export, the observatory snapshot and page, the driver's report, and a manifest with every file's digest. Nothing in a run directory is edited after the run; the table below is read from those files.

## Layout

```
data/proving-ground/
  <date>-<implementer>-run-<n>/
    manifest.json        repository head, composition, implementer, session ids, per-file bytes and SHA-256
    result.json          the driver's report: fleet report, delegation records, export reports, observatory document
    facts.jsonl          scorekeeper facts, one per cell session
    trajectories.jsonl   curator-gated trajectory export, one per exported session
    observatory.json     the observatory snapshot the page was rendered from
    observatory.html     the rendered observatory page
    sessions/            the cell session logs, one JSONL file per cell, named by session id
```

## Running one

A run is a Loader-booted composition under `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/` driven from an empty directory outside the repository; the driver creates the session store there and writes the exports next to it. The first run used the composition below, with the host's own Claude Code installation and account as the implementer of every cell:

```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/proving-ground-run && cd /tmp/proving-ground-run
REPO=/path/to/deepseek-harness
TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH=$REPO/tsconfig.json node --import $REPO/node_modules/tsx/dist/esm/index.mjs $REPO/examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/village-claude-implementer/driver.ts $REPO/examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/village-claude-implementer/cordis.yml > stdout.jsonl
```

Then record it, which copies the exports, every session log, and the driver's result into a new run directory, writes its `manifest.json` with the repository head, the composition, the implementers read from the run stamps, and every file's digest, and refuses to overwrite a recorded run; add a row below afterwards:

```sh
node data/proving-ground/tools/record-run.mjs /tmp/proving-ground-run 2026-09-06-claude-code-run-2 --composition examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/village-live/cordis.yml
```

A live district (`examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/village-live/`) is recorded the same way from the directory its driver runs in, one slot per run directory: the shift ledger session lands beside the cell sessions and `result.json` holds the driver's status.

## What a row proves

A delegated cell's certificate proves that the runner authored the standard before any work started, restored the immutable paths from the fixture over the tree the external agent left, found the check-owned set unchanged, and ran the checks itself. It proves nothing about how the work was done: the external agent's prompts, tool calls, and reasoning stay in its own product, so the cell session holds the stamp, the standard, the delegation records, the runs, and the certificate, and no assistant turn. The exported trajectory therefore carries no step. It is a measurement, not training data, and the `implementer` field on the stamp is what a curated export filters on. The [external implementer note](../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-06-external-implementer.md) owns these rules.

The fourth record is the Proving Ground bench's first fleet (`examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/proving-ground-bench/`, thirty admitted program tasks): the product's own loop as the implementer of every cell, over the six tier-2 environments that are not held out, two repetitions each, seed 1, policy `bench-2026-09-07`, district `bench-h1`, two cells at a time, 984 s of wall time for the twelve cells. Every cell was certified in one attempt, so tier 2 is a ceiling for this implementer and the paired comparisons between the harness loop and the product loop run on tiers 3 and 4. The cells name the model `sonnet`; the product ran the installation's default model, which was measured as sonnet immediately before the run, because the delegation did not yet forward the cell's model to the child (the slice that forwards it and records the child's reported model is queued). The bench composition and tasks are those of commit `128e037bb`; the manifest records the head of the working tree at recording time.

+## Layout
+
+```
+data/proving-ground/

+    trajectories.jsonl   curator-gated trajectory export, one per exported session
+    observatory.json     the observatory snapshot the page was rendered from
+    observatory.html     the rendered observatory page
+    sessions/            the cell session logs, one JSONL file per cell, named by session id
+```
+
+## Running one
+
+A run is a Loader-booted composition under `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/` driven from an empty directory outside the repository; the driver creates the session store there and writes the exports next to it. The first run used the composition below, with the host's own Claude Code installation and account as the implementer of every cell:
+
+```sh
+mkdir -p /tmp/proving-ground-run && cd /tmp/proving-ground-run
+REPO=/path/to/deepseek-harness
+TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH=$REPO/tsconfig.json node --import $REPO/node_modules/tsx/dist/esm/index.mjs $REPO/examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/village-claude-implementer/driver.ts $REPO/examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/village-claude-implementer/cordis.yml > stdout.jsonl
+```
+
+Then record it, which copies the exports, every session log, and the driver's result into a new run directory, writes its `manifest.json` with the repository head, the composition, the implementers read from the run stamps, and every file's digest, and refuses to overwrite a recorded run; add a row below afterwards:
+

+```

+
+## What a row proves
+
+A delegated cell's certificate proves that the runner authored the standard before any work started, restored the immutable paths from the fixture over the tree the external agent left, found the check-owned set unchanged, and ran the checks itself. # Proving Ground 运行记录

[English](README.md) | 中文

真实 Proving Ground 运行的记录：该区对一个实现者（implementer）在已注册环境上的经认证测量，完全按 harness 折叠和导出的原样保存。一个运行目录就是一次 fleet 计划的输出：cell 会话日志、导出的会话事实、经 curator 把关的 trajectory 导出、observatory 快照与页面、驱动器的报告，以及带有每个文件摘要的 manifest。运行目录中的任何内容在运行之后都不再编辑；下表由这些文件读出。

## Layout

```
data/proving-ground/
  <date>-<implementer>-run-<n>/
    manifest.json        repository head, composition, implementer, session ids, per-file bytes and SHA-256
    result.json          the driver's report: fleet report, delegation records, export reports, observatory document
    facts.jsonl          scorekeeper facts, one per cell session
    trajectories.jsonl   curator-gated trajectory export, one per exported session
    observatory.json     the observatory snapshot the page was rendered from
    observatory.html     the rendered observatory page
    sessions/            the cell session logs, one JSONL file per cell, named by session id
```

## 运行一次

@@ -0,0 +1,90 @@
+# Proving Ground runs
+
+English | [中文](README.zh.md)
+
+Records of real Proving Ground runs: the district's certified measurements of one implementer on registered environments, kept exactly as the harness folded and exported them. A run directory is the output of one fleet plan: the cell session logs, the exported session facts, the curator-gated trajectory export, the observatory snapshot and page, the driver's report, and a manifest with every file's digest. Nothing in a run directory is edited after the run; the table below is read from those files.
+
+## Layout
+
+```
+data/proving-ground/
+  <date>-<implementer>-run-<n>/
+    manifest.json        repository head, composition, implementer, session ids, per-file bytes and SHA-256
+    result.json          the driver's report: fleet report, delegation records, export reports, observatory document
+    facts.jsonl          scorekeeper facts, one per cell session
+    trajectories.jsonl   curator-gated trajectory export, one per exported session
+    observatory.json     the observatory snapshot the page was rendered from
+    observatory.html     the rendered observatory page
+    sessions/            the cell session logs, one JSONL file per cell, named by session id
+```
+
+## Running one
+
+A run is a Loader-booted composition under `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/` driven from an empty directory outside the repository; the driver creates the session store there and writes the exports next to it. The first run used the composition below, with the host's own Claude Code installation and account as the implementer of every cell:
+
+```sh
+mkdir -p /tmp/proving-ground-run && cd /tmp/proving-ground-run
+REPO=/path/to/deepseek-harness
+TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH=$REPO/tsconfig.json node --import $REPO/node_modules/tsx/dist/esm/index.mjs $REPO/examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/village-claude-implementer/driver.ts $REPO/examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/village-claude-implementer/cordis.yml > stdout.jsonl
+```
+
+Then record it, which copies the exports, every session log, and the driver's result into a new run directory, writes its `manifest.json` with the repository head, the composition, the implementers read from the run stamps, and every file's digest, and refuses to overwrite a recorded run; add a row below afterwards:
+
+```sh
+node data/proving-ground/tools/record-run.mjs /tmp/proving-ground-run 2026-09-06-claude-code-run-2 --composition examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/village-live/cordis.yml
+```
+
+A live district (`examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/village-live/`) is recorded the same way from the directory its driver runs in, one slot per run directory: the shift ledger session lands beside the cell sessions and `result.json` holds the driver's status.
+
+## What a row proves
+
+A delegated cell's certificate proves that the runner authored the standard before any work started, restored the immutable paths from the fixture over the tree the external agent left, found the check-owned set unchanged, and ran the checks itself. It proves nothing about how the work was done: the external agent's prompts, tool calls, and reasoning stay in its own product, so the cell session holds the stamp, the standard, the delegation records, the runs, and the certificate, and no assistant turn. The exported trajectory therefore carries no step. It is a measurement, not training data, and the `implementer` field on the stamp is what a curated export filters on. The [external implementer note](../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-06-external-implementer.md) owns these rules.

# Proving Ground 运行记录

[English](README.md) | 中文

真实 Proving Ground 运行的记录：该区对一个实现者（implementer）在已注册环境上的经认证测量，完全按 harness 折叠和导出的原样保存。一个运行目录就是一次 fleet 计划的输出：cell 会话日志、导出的会话事实、经 curator 把关的 trajectory 导出、observatory 快照与页面、驱动器的报告，以及带有每个文件摘要的 manifest。运行目录中的任何内容在运行之后都不再编辑；下表由这些文件读出。

## Layout

```
data/proving-ground/
  <date>-<implementer>-run-<n>/
    manifest.json        repository head, composition, implementer, session ids, per-file bytes and SHA-256
    result.json          the driver's report: fleet report, delegation records, export reports, observatory document
    facts.jsonl          scorekeeper facts, one per cell session
    trajectories.jsonl   curator-gated trajectory export, one per exported session
    observatory.json     the observatory snapshot the page was rendered from
    observatory.html     the rendered observatory page
    sessions/            the cell session logs, one JSONL file per cell, named by session id
```

## 运行一次

一次运行是 `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/` 下的一个由 Loader 启动的组合，从仓库之外的一个空目录驱动；驱动器在那里创建会话存储，并把导出写在它旁边。第一次运行使用了下面的组合，以宿主机自己的 Claude Code 安装和账户作为每个 cell 的实现者：

```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/proving-ground-run && cd /tmp/proving-ground-run
REPO=/path/to/deepseek-harness
TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH=$REPO/tsconfig.json node --import $REPO/node_modules/tsx/dist/esm/index.mjs $REPO/examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/village-claude-implementer/driver.ts $REPO/examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/village-claude-implementer/cordis.yml > stdout.jsonl
```

然后记录它：该工具把导出、每份会话日志和驱动器的结果复制到一个新的运行目录，写出带有仓库 head、组合、从运行 stamp 读出的实现者以及每个文件摘要的 `manifest.json`，并拒绝覆盖已记录的运行；之后再在下表中加一行：

```sh
node data/proving-ground/tools/record-run.mjs /tmp/proving-ground-run 2026-09-06-claude-code-run-2 --composition examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/village-live/cordis.yml
```

实时区（`examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/village-live/`）以同样方式从其驱动器运行所在的目录记录，每个时槽一个运行目录：班次账本会话与 cell 会话并排落地，`result.json` 保存驱动器的状态。

## 一行证明了什么

一个被委托的 cell 的证书证明：runner 在任何工作开始之前就编写了标准，在外部 agent 留下的目录树上从 fixture 恢复了不可变路径，确认由检查拥有的文件集未被改动，并亲自运行了检查。它不证明工作是如何完成的：外部 agent 的提示、工具调用和推理都留在它自己的产品里，因此 cell 会话只保存 stamp、标准、委托记录、运行和证书，而没有任何助手轮次。导出的 trajectory 因此不含任何步骤。它是一次测量，而不是训练数据，stamp 上的 `implementer` 字段就是经策展的导出所要过滤的依据。[外部实现者说明](../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-06-external-implementer.md)拥有这些规则。

+mkdir -p /tmp/proving-ground-run && cd /tmp/proving-ground-run

+```

+## 一行证明了什么
+
+一个被委托的 cell 的证书证明：runner 在任何工作开始之前就编写了标准，在外部 agent 留下的目录树上从 fixture 恢复了不可变路径，确认由检查拥有的文件集未被改动，并亲自运行了检查。它不证明工作是如何完成的：外部 agent 的提示、工具调用和推理都留在它自己的产品里，因此 cell 会话只保存 stamp、标准、委托记录、运行和证书，而没有任何助手轮次。导出的 trajectory 因此不含任何步骤。它是一次测量，而不是训练数据，stamp 上的 `implementer` 字段就是经策展的导出所要过滤的依据。[外部实现者说明](../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-06-external-implementer.md)拥有这些规则。

Keep every behaviour the passing tests already pin down, keep the exported names `parse`, `matches`, `next` and `CronError`, and do not weaken the module by special-casing the inputs the tests happen to use.\n\n`parse(expression)` takes five whitespace-separated fields — minute 0 to 59, hour 0 to 23, day of month 1 to 31, month 1 to 12, day of week 0 to 7 — and returns the values each field admits as a sorted array without duplicates, alongside `restrictedDayOfMonth` and `restrictedDayOfWeek`, which are false only when that field is written as a bare `*`. A field is a comma-separated list of terms, and a term is `*`, a single value, `a-b`, or any of those followed by `/step`, where `*/s` walks the whole field, `a-b/s` walks the range and `a/s` walks from `a` to the field maximum. A step always counts from the start of the range it applies to. Months accept `JAN` to `DEC` and days of the week `SUN` to `SAT`, in any case, including inside a range, and 7 means Sunday, so it is the same value as 0.\n\n`matches(expression, date)` reports whether the expression fires during that UTC minute, ignoring seconds. `next(expression, from)` returns the first matching minute strictly after `from`, as a `Date` with zero seconds, and throws when there is none within five years. Both use UTC throughout and the Gregorian calendar, so a year is a leap year when it is divisible by 4 and either not divisible by 100 or divisible by 400. When both day fields are restricted a day is scheduled if either one accepts it; when only one is restricted only that one applies.\n\nFailures throw `CronError`: `expected 5 fields, got 4`, `value 60 is out of range 0-59 in minute`, `unknown name FOO in month`, `invalid step 0 in minute`, `range 5-1 is reversed in minute`, `invalid value a in minute`, `empty value in dayOfWeek`, `invalid range 1-2-3 in minute`, `invalid term 1/2/3 in minute`, `expression must be a string`, `date must be a valid Date`, `from must be a valid Date` and `no occurrence within 5 years`.",
  "heldOut": false,
  "immutable": [
    "test",
    "package.json"
  ],
  "checks": [
    {
      "id": "tests-pass",
      "outcome": "the test suite passes",
      "run": "node --test test/*.test.js"
    },
    {
      "id": "no-dependencies",
      "outcome": "no packages were installed",
      "run": "test ! -e node_modules"
    }
  ]
}

60	/** What one case feeds the candidate. */
61	export interface CheckCaseInput {
62	  /**
63	   * Command words appended to the check's run instruction. Each word must need
64	   * no shell quoting, because the composed shell's dialect is not known here.
65	   */
66	  readonly argv: readonly string[]
67	  /** Bytes written to the candidate's stdin, which is then closed; absent leaves stdin empty. */
68	  readonly stdin?: string
69	  /** UTF-8 files staged into the workspace before the case runs, keyed by normalized workspace-relative path. */
70	  readonly files?: Readonly<Record<string, string>>
71	}
72	
73	/** Digests one case compares its configured channels against. */
74	export interface CheckCaseExpectation {
75	  /** Exit code the candidate must report, for a case comparing `exit`. */
76	  readonly exitCode?: number
77	  /** SHA-256 hex of the normalized stdout bytes, for a case comparing `stdout`. */
78	  readonly stdoutSha256?: string
79	  /** SHA-256 hex of the normalized stderr bytes, for a case comparing `stderr`. */
80	  readonly stderrSha256?: string
81	  /** SHA-256 hex of the normalized work tree under `treeScope`, for a case comparing `tree`. */
82	  readonly treeSha256?: string
83	}
84	
85	/** How one case decides that a channel agrees. */
86	export interface CheckCaseComparator {
87	  /** Non-empty channel set, without repeats; the case passes only when every one of them matches. */
88	  readonly channels: readonly CheckCaseChannel[]
89	  /** Normalizers applied to each compared byte channel, in this order. */
90	  readonly normalizers: readonly CheckCaseNormalizer[]
91	}
92	
93	/** One behavioural sample of a check: what the candidate is fed and what it must produce. */
94	export interface CheckCase {
95	  /** Lower-kebab-case identity unique inside the owning check. */
96	  readonly id: CheckCaseId
97	  /** Positive safe-integer share of the check's weight this case carries. */
98	  readonly weight: number
99	  /** What the case feeds the candidate. */
100	  readonly input: CheckCaseInput
101	  /** Digests the case's configured channels are compared against. */
102	  readonly expected: CheckCaseExpectation
103	  /** Channels compared and the normalizers applied before comparison. */
104	  readonly comparator: CheckCaseComparator
105	}
106	
107	/**
108	 * The durable reference to one check's case bodies. The bodies live in the
109	 * validator's reservation, never in the session log; `sha256` binds the two.
110	 */
111	export interface CheckCasesRef {
112	  /** Number of cases the bodies hold. */
113	  readonly count: number
114	  /** Sum of every case weight. */
115	  readonly weightTotal: number
116	  /** SHA-256 hex of the canonical case bodies. */
117	  readonly sha256: string
118	}
119	
120	/** One executable check: the outcome it establishes and how a validator runs it. */
121	export interface StandardCheck {
122	  /** Lower-kebab-case identity unique inside the owning standard. */
123	  readonly id: CheckId
124	  /** Outcome the task must establish, stated without the implementation. */
125	  readonly outcome: string
126	  /** Validator-owned execution instruction (command line or procedure). */
127	  readonly run: string
128	  /** Reference to the check's case bodies; absent for a check whose verdict is its own exit code. */
129	  readonly cases?: CheckCasesRef
130	  /**
131	   * Normalized workspace-relative directory the `tree` channel digests, which
132	   * the runner empties before each case that compares it. Present exactly when
133	   * a case compares `tree`.
134	   */
135	  readonly treeScope?: string
136	}
137	
138	/**
139	 * One check as its author hands it in. The case bodies travel with the check
140	 * only to authorship, which validates them against {@link StandardCheck.cases}
141	 * and stores the reference alone: the log carries no case body.
142	 */
143	export interface AuthoredCheck extends StandardCheck {
144	  /** Complete case bodies; required exactly when `cases` is present. */
145	  readonly caseBodies?: readonly CheckCase[]
146	}
147	
148	/** A check removed from the active set together with its unsatisfiability evidence. */
149	export interface RelaxedCheck {
150	  /** The exact check that was removed. */
151	  readonly check: StandardCheck
152	  /** Recorded evidence that the stricter form is unsatisfiable. */
153	  readonly evidence: string
154	}

169	/**

1	/**
2	 * Producer: the Proving Ground bench's environments, one per
3	 * `environments/<task>/task.json`. The task directory is the fixture: `src/`
4	 * is the pre-state the implementer receives, `test/` and `package.json` are
5	 * immutable, and `reference/` holds the solution a validator may run and an
6	 * implementer never sees. Tier and domain travel in the definition's detail so
7	 * a plan can select cells by them.
8	 */
9	
10	import { existsSync, readdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
11	import { join } from 'node:path'
12	import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'
13	import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
14	import { EnvironmentId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments'
15	import type { EnvironmentDefinition } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments'
16	import { CheckId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-verification'
17	
18	declare module '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments/types' {
19	  interface EnvironmentKindMap {
20	    /** A bench task in one language, verified by its fixture's own test suite, with the bench's tier and domain. */
21	    bench: { readonly language: string; readonly tier: number; readonly domain: string }
22	  }
23	}
24	
25	export const name = 'register-environments'
26	export const inject = ['environments']
27	
28	/** The fields `task.json` carries, as the authoring specification defines them. */
29	interface TaskFile {
30	  readonly id: string
31	  readonly tier: number
32	  readonly domain: string
33	  readonly title: string
34	  readonly prompt: string
35	  readonly heldOut: boolean
36	  readonly immutable: readonly string[]
37	  readonly checks: readonly { readonly id: string; readonly outcome: string; readonly run: string }[]
38	}
39	
40	const ROOT = fileURLToPath(new URL('./environments/', import.meta.url))
41	const OWNER = 'headless-agent proving-ground-bench fixture'
42	
43	/** The rules every task shares: only `src/` changes, the tests and the manifest stay, nothing gets installed. */
44	const SHARED_RULES = 'Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.'
45	
46	/** One bench task, read from its directory. */
47	function definition(directory: string): EnvironmentDefinition<'bench'> {
48	  const fixture = join(ROOT, directory)
49	  const task = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(fixture, 'task.json'), 'utf8')) as TaskFile
50	  if (task.id !== `code:${directory}`) throw new Error(`proving-ground-bench: ${directory}/task.json declares id ${task.id}`)
51	  return {
52	    id: EnvironmentId(task.id),
53	    kind: 'bench',
54	    name: task.title,
55	    description: `${task.domain}, tier ${task.tier}: ${task.title}`,
56	    task: {
57	      prompt: `${task.prompt} ${SHARED_RULES}`,
58	      fixture,
59	      immutable: task.immutable,
60	      ...(existsSync(join(fixture, 'reference')) ? { reference: 'reference' } : {}),
61	    },
62	    checks: task.checks.map(check => ({ id: CheckId(check.id), outcome: check.outcome, run: check.run })),
63	    heldOut: task.heldOut,
64	    owner: OWNER,
65	    provenance: 'curated',
66	    detail: { language: 'javascript', tier: task.tier, domain: task.domain },
67	  }
68	}
69	
70	/**
71	 * Register every task directory under the producer's own fiber; a bench with no
72	 * task is a misconfiguration and fails the boot.
73	 * @param ctx - the plugin context carrying the environment registry.
74	 */
75	export function apply(ctx: Context): void {
76	  const directories = existsSync(ROOT)
77	    ? readdirSync(ROOT, { withFileTypes: true })
78	      .filter(entry => entry.isDirectory() && existsSync(join(ROOT, entry.name, 'task.json')))
79	      .map(entry => entry.name)
80	      .sort()
81	    : []
82	  if (directories.length === 0) throw new Error(`proving-ground-bench: no environments/<task>/task.json under ${ROOT}`)
83	  for (const directory of directories) ctx.effect(() => ctx.environments.register(definition(directory)))
84	}

1	#!/usr/bin/env node
2	/**
3	 * Admission of the bench's environments: for every `environments/<task>/`,
4	 * the fixture as shipped must fail its own tests (the pre-state), the hidden
5	 * reference must pass them, no `node_modules` may exist, and `task.json` must
6	 * carry the fields the registrar reads. Exits 1 on the first task that fails
7	 * admission; prints one line per admitted task.
8	 *
9	 *   node admit.mjs [<environments-dir>]
10	 */
11	
12	import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process'
13	import { cpSync, existsSync, mkdtempSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, rmSync } from 'node:fs'
14	import { tmpdir } from 'node:os'
15	import { join, resolve } from 'node:path'
16	import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'
17	
18	const root = resolve(process.argv[2] ?? fileURLToPath(new URL('./environments/', import.meta.url)))
19	const REQUIRED = ['id', 'tier', 'domain', 'title', 'prompt', 'heldOut', 'immutable', 'checks']
20	
21	function runTests(cwd) {
22	  return spawnSync('node', ['--test', 'test/*.test.js'], { cwd, encoding: 'utf8', shell: true, timeout: 120_000 })
23	}
24	
25	let failures = 0
26	for (const name of readdirSync(root).sort()) {
27	  const dir = join(root, name)
28	  const taskPath = join(dir, 'task.json')
29	  if (!existsSync(taskPath)) continue
30	  const task = JSON.parse(readFileSync(taskPath, 'utf8'))
31	  const missing = REQUIRED.filter(field => !(field in task))
32	  const problems = []
33	  if (missing.length > 0) problems.push(`task.json lacks ${missing.join(', ')}`)
34	  if (task.id !== `code:${name}`) problems.push(`id ${task.id} does not match directory ${name}`)
35	  if (existsSync(join(dir, 'node_modules'))) problems.push('node_modules present')
36	  if (!existsSync(join(dir, 'reference', 'src'))) problems.push('no reference/src')
37	  const copy = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), `admit-${name}-`))
38	  try {
39	    cpSync(dir, copy, { recursive: true })
40	    rmSync(join(copy, 'reference'), { recursive: true, force: true })
41	    const pre = runTests(copy)
42	    if (pre.status === 0) problems.push('pre-state passes its tests')
43	    rmSync(join(copy, 'src'), { recursive: true, force: true })
44	    cpSync(join(dir, 'reference', 'src'), join(copy, 'src'), { recursive: true })
45	    const ref = runTests(copy)
46	    if (ref.status !== 0) problems.push(`reference fails its tests: ${(ref.stdout + ref.stderr).split('\n').filter(line => /not ok|Error/.test(line)).slice(0, 3).join(' | ')}`)
47	  } finally {
48	    rmSync(copy, { recursive: true, force: true })
49	  }
50	  if (problems.length > 0) {
51	    failures += 1
52	    console.error(`REJECT ${name}: ${problems.join('; ')}`)
53	  } else {
54	    console.log(`admit ${task.id} tier=${task.tier} domain=${task.domain} heldOut=${task.heldOut}`)
55	  }
56	}
57	if (failures > 0) {
58	  console.error(`admit: ${failures} task(s) rejected`)
59	  process.exit(1)
60	}
